#2769. Lakers rookie forward leaves no doubt he can play with Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves

Lakers rookie forward leaves no doubt he can play with Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

LOS ANGELES – When the Los Angeles Lakers began NBA Summer League play, they had all three of their available two-way contract slots filled. But once game play got underway, Arthur Kaluma forced the Lakers to make a quick decision.

Arthur Kaluma made a big impact during summer league for the Lakers, and instead of allowing another team to scoop him up, they quickly signed him to a two-way contract while waiving undrafted rookie guard Peter Suder in the process. The 24-year-old is no stranger to the organization. He went undrafted himself in 2025 and latched on with the Lakers' G League affiliate after spending training camp and preseason with the team.

He is, however, a rookie to the NBA and it's not yet certain how much opportunity he'll actually get with the Lakers this season. What is certain is that he will get plenty of live game reps in the G League with the Coachella Valley Lakers. Although he'll be granted a higher level of freedom on the court in the G League, he knows he has to focus on specific things to be able to run alongside Laker stars Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"My defensive versatility. I can guard one through five, and my ability to make open shots and create on offense," Kaluma said during Coachella Valley Media Day on Nov. 2. "That's good, but when you're playing with guys like Luka and AR, the ball is not going to be in your hands as much. So my off-ball creation is gonna be good. My ability to set screens and most definitely my ability to guard."

Kaluma has yet to see action in an NBA game yet, but he did appear in one preseason game with the Lakers this year. During summer league was where he really shined. He suited up in seven games across both the California Classic and Las Vegas, averaging a little north of 17 points per game.

He shot 55.1 percent from the field, 38.9 percent from the 3-point line and 79.2 percent from the free-throw line. Having spent his first year as a pro within the Lakers' system, he already has familiarity and comfort. The Lakers' new G League head coach, Alex Cerda, was on staff last season as an assistant under Zach Guthrie.

And when it comes to getting G League reps, Kaluma believes that it has become a legitimate training ground for players hoping to break through to the NBA.

"Definitely, if you approach it the correct way. It's an opportunity for you to get better," Kaluma said. "And so every single time I come down here or every time I'm gonna be playing in the G League, my main focus is working on the things that are gonna help translate to an NBA court."

On a two-way contract, Kaluma is limited to the number of appearances he can make in the NBA. He's already been active for a couple of Lakers games this season albeit not seeing any playing time. That still counts as part of his 50-game maximum.

One of the things players on two-way contracts find themselves having to get used to is the shuffle back and forth between the NBA and the G League. Injuries and absences can happen in the blink of an eye, calling those players into immediate duty with their NBA team.

Since the G League season began on Nov. 6, Kaluma has spent the entire time with Coachella Valley. But he knows the day might come when his number is called, and potentially without warning. And so he is doing the best he can to keep himself fresh and ready to go at a moment's notice.

"That's pretty much it, you gotta stay ready," Kaluma said. "I can play a game here and they can call me back and I have to go fly out somewhere and play a game with the main team. So just always being ready and waiting for my number to be called. Just stay consistent and level-headed mentally throughout it all is probably going to be the best thing I can do."

#2765. Without Steph Curry, Warriors rookie is going to be put to ultimate test

Yaxel Lendeborg has never lacked confidence.

When the Warriors were in the running to acquire LeBron James, the rookie expressed excitement about potentially playing alongside one of the greatest players of all time but also told the California Post, "Hopefully he doesn't take away my minutes."

And after Lendeborg and Luka Doncic exchanged trash talk when the Lakers played the Warriors in their season opener, Lendeborg said he "lost all respect" for one of the NBA's biggest superstars, calling out his "whining" and "complaining."

After Steph Curry suffered an oblique abdominal tear in the Warriors' 115-108 loss to the Rockets on Wednesday, Lendeborg is now the team's star.

Curry will be reevaluated in two weeks and is expected to be sidelined close to a month, according to ESPN, meaning it's now up to the 24-year-old to carry the franchise.

And so far he has walked the walk, averaging 21.7 points, 7.4 rebounds and 3.7 assists while surging to the top of the Rookie of the Year race.

That's a different challenge altogether. We're really about to see what Lendeborg is capable of, especially considering Curry had opened the season playing out of his mind.

The 38-year-old Curry was having an MVP-caliber campaign, entering Wednesday's game averaging 30.6 points, 4.3 assists and 4.1 rebounds for the Warriors, who had stunned the league by winning eight straight games.

Golden State Warriors player Steph Curry attends the season opener against the Los Angeles Lakers in Los Angeles on Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026. London Entertainment

Overnight, Lendeborg has gone from being a sidekick to the main character.

Draymond Green said he already saw glimmers of that happening Wednesday.

"It's funny because the thing that he's going to have to learn and understand is, all right, Steph wasn't out there, KD (Kevin Durant) was off the court, you look around, you're probably the best player on the floor," Green told reporters. "Regardless of team.

"I think there was a point he realized, ding, ding, ding, and he started attacking, and the game flipped for us. I think that's something that he's going to have to realize really fast. There will be oftentimes where he can possibly be the best player on the floor regardless of the team. We need him to show that. He doesn't have a problem doing it."

Lendeborg has been one of the season's biggest stories.

Golden State Warriors player Yaxel Lendeborg, left, and head coach Steve Kerr smile during a game against the Houston Rockets on Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images

The Warriors' 11th pick in the draft breathed new life into Curry's career during what was thought to be a lost season after Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody suffered injuries that would sideline them for the first few months and Kristaps Porzingis announced he was stepping away from basketball indefinitely.

Lendeborg picked up the slack. Brandin Podziemski is making major contributions, averaging career highs in points (17.3), field-goal percentage (48.1) and 3-point shooting (39.7%). And Green is capable of bottling up anyone in the league on any given night.

The person who's going to feel that most is Lendeborg, who's going to experience a different type of defensive pressure than he's ever seen.

Curry is a four-time MVP. He carried the Warriors to four championships in eight years from 2015-2022 before the dynasty began flailing, failing to advance past the second round of the playoffs the last four years.

Lendeborg helped resuscitate Golden State. Now he's going to have to put it on his shoulders.

Lendeborg wants that. He wants to be a star. But can he handle it now?

Golden State Warriors forward Yaxel Lendeborg (1) shoots against Houston Rockets forward Kevin Durant (7) in Houston, Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026. AP Photo/Ashley Landis

Green made waves at the top of the season for saying the Warriors found the "next face of the franchise" in Lendeborg. That meant a lot coming from Green, who doesn't give that type of praise easily, especially to a rookie.

We're going to get a preview of whether he was right. Whether Lendeborg is ready. Whether he's able to handle the pressure.

Last season, the Warriors went 13-26 without Curry, who missed 27 straight games because of runner's knee.

They're better equipped to deal with Curry's absence this time around because of an outspoken and talented rookie who's about to be thrust into a situation he was supposed to be eased into.

For however long Curry is out, Lendeborg is the face of the Warriors.

His confidence is going to be put to the ultimate test.

#2763. DeMarvion Overshown didn't know inactive players couldn't celebrate on the field

The Cowboys had 14 accepted penalties for 153 yards in the 27-23 win over the Colts. One of them was called unacceptable and undisciplined by Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones.

Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who was inactive and dressed in street clothes, came onto the field to celebrate after Quinnen Williams forced a Jonathan Taylor fumble that Shemar James returned to the Dallas 30. Overshown was penalized 15 yards, with referee Clay Martin saying, “After the play, unsportsmanlike conduct by Dallas. We have non-uniformed player in blue sweats and a stocking cap come onto the field to celebrate. That’s a 15-yard penalty.”

Overshown apologized to head coach Brian Schottenheimer and his teammates.

“At the end of the day, I talked to Schotty about it,” Overshown said Thursday, via Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News. “I apologized about it. It was definitely in the moment, but earlier I had said that as a defense, we’re going to start celebrating more, getting takeaways. And I was just caught in the moment. So you can laugh at it now, because we won the game, but in the moment, fourth quarter, tied ball game or close ball game, you don’t want a 15-yard penalty from a guy, especially that’s not even playing. So that’s a lesson learned.”

Overshown said he didn’t know the rule until linebacker Dee Winters started yelling at him, which should prompt questions about why Overshown didn’t know the rule. But he defended Schottenheimer and said he accepted his “butt chewing.”

“It’s not an indictment on Schotty. It’s on me as a player. I own it,” he said.

Skattebo's numbers at the half: eight carries for 35 yards and a touchdown, plus two catches for 37 yards.

Skattebo's 1-yard touchdown dive put the Giants up 7-3 with 2:35 left in the half. The Commanders immediately answered with a 67-yard touchdown drive.

Skattebo and quarterback J.J. McCarthy combined for a highlight-worthy moment on third-and-7 in the first quarter. Before getting hauled down, McCarthy flipped an underhanded pass to Skattebo, who sprinted for a wild 34-yard play that moved the Giants to Washington's 21.

But the drive ended with Dominic Zvada's missed 33-yard field goal, keeping the game scoreless.

These were Skattebo's numbers at the end of the first quarter: three carries for 23 yards, with a long of 14, and two catches on three targets for 37 yards. An encouraging start, thanks to that 34-yard gem.

Skattebo arrived Thursday night at MetLife Stadium and walked into the locker room wearing a Giants-themed "Iron Man" helmet/mask. He clearly was trying to make the point that he can handle a hefty workload — especially on a night with sloppy weather conditions.

After Harbaugh this week opted to not trade for Taylor, Skattebo insisted he has what it takes to thrive as a No. 1 back in the NFL.

The past month has been eventful for him, to say the least.

On Oct. 11 in Washington, his fumble (on a wet day) cost the Giants a likely overtime win. (They were lucky to escape with a tie.) A week later, Harbaugh benched Skattebo, plagued by ball security woes, against the Saints.

In the next game, Skattebo responded by running for 124 yards and a touchdown in a massive overtime win at Houston. But he hurt his hamstring on his final run that day, so he missed last week's post-bye week win in Philadelphia, site of his devastating ankle injury last year.

Against the Eagles — with Skattebo and Tyrone Tracy sidelined — the Giants' running game sputtered, as Devin Singletary managed just 31 yards on 21 carries.

Skattebo made his return — without having to worry about being replaced (at least during the season) — on Thursday night against Washington.

He wanted to show Harbaugh — with a Houston-like gem — that he didn't need to revisit the Taylor situation next offseason.

This is a massive game for the 5-2-1 Giants, who lead the 4-5 Cowboys and 2-5-1 Commanders in the flawed NFC East.

Harbaugh is trying to improve to 5-1-1 without quarterback Jaxson Dart (including 3-0 with J.J. McCarthy as Dart's replacement) and 3-0-1 overall in division play.

The Giants entered Thursday having polished off three (really, four) one-score wins since Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 2, underscoring their newfound late-game resilience with Harbaugh.

Since the Cowboys have a challenging game against the 49ers this weekend, the Giants could emerge from this week's games in complete control of the division.

Giants blow shot to take control of NFC East with shocking late collapse vs. Commanders Nov. 13, 2026, 12:12 a.m.

Giants are winning games under John Harbaugh they used to lose. Here's what changedNov. 12, 2026, 1:06 p.m.

Plus, this franchise hasn't won three straight games since 2023.

The Giants won just 13 total games over the past three years. They last captured their division in 2011.

As they chase the NFC East crown this year, Thursday is a critical game for head-to-head tiebreaker purposes, since they tied Washington in the teams' first matchup.

#2742. NBA’s anti-tanking rules ironically tanking Utah Jazz season

I know that sports fans have said, "This is our year," at the beginning of every season for every sport since the dawn of man. Archaeologists only recently discovered cave drawings of ancient man calling his shot by prematurely tattooing the Larry O'Brien Trophy on his shoulder with the description: "Tigris River Valley Hunter-Gatherers 5,000 B.C. World Champions" (no need to fact-check me on this, just trust me).

But for the Utah Jazz, the 2026-27 season was actually supposed to be "their year". No blind optimism, no baseless fantasies. Just grounded, reasonable, and logical projections for a team on the rise.

Through four painful seasons, the Jazz lost a grand total of 211 games in search of an elusive young superstar to lift their tragic franchise from an endless tank. As those four seasons came to a close, Utah finally claimed their prize: a star guard out of Kansas named Darryn Peterson. And he couldn't have come at a better time, either.

Tired of witnessing one-third of the league actively trying to lose basketball games, the NBA enacted anti-tanking protocols and installed lottery reform intent on de-incentivizing the act of "tanking".

Teams have far less incentive to tank this season, especially this early on, as the owners of the four worst records will have a statistically lower chance of getting the number-one overall pick than those who finish 5th-8th from the bottom.

That adjustment is one of two reasons why Utah is off to such a slow start. The other, in my view, is having a very injured roster at a time when most teams are still playing at or near full strength. Teams are fighting to win every game, and the Jazz are ill-equipped to fight back.

As a result, the Jazz are off to an even worse start this year through 11 games than any of their rebuilding seasons. They hold hands at the bottom of the Western Conference standings with an abysmal Sacramento team.

2022-23: 8-32023-24: 4-72024-25: 3-82025-26: 4-72026-27: 1-11

The Jazz are not tanking. Not intentionally, anyway.

Utah has even less reason to minimize their competitive edge, being barred from a top-four pick after drafting second overall this summer, and owing their pick to Memphis even if it were to finish in a favorable position.

With three of their five starters out with prolonged injuries, things may get even worse before they get any better. But they can — and I believe Utah will — improve before a play-in spot is out of reach.

Assuming Lauri Markkanen, Jaren Jackson Jr. and Jusuf Nurkic all return according to current timetables, the Jazz are only a month or two away from full strength, barring further injury. This is a team still learning to play with each other. With several key pieces having arrived within the last year, chemistry will take time to develop.

A Play-In appearance is a reasonable goal this season, despite my own preseason projections anticipating a top-six finish. Should the Jazz rally and finish with a top-10 record in the Western Conference, Utah has hope of building on that success in the following season. This was never going to be "the year" for Utah. It was always destined to be a stepping stone. But so long as that stride carries the Jazz closer to a better place, there's still reason for optimism.

This is a talented team. Time will tell if talent can translate to results.

Calvin Barrett is the Associate Editor for SLC Dunk and a Utah Jazz columnist for the Standard-Examiner. Originally from Springville, Utah, he currently writes from his desk in Japan.

After reaching 214/3 at the 30-over mark, New Zealand managed just 51 runs while losing three crucial wickets between overs 31 and 40 to finish Powerplay 2 at 265/6.

Axar Patel struck immediately in the 31st over (30.2 ov) to remove a dangerous Finn Allen (41 off 30) caught by Rohit Sharma, to wrap up a superb spell of 10-0-39-2.

After guiding New Zealand past 250 in 36.2 overs, Will Young fell on the final ball of the 37th over (36.6 ov) for 125 off 108 balls (14 fours, 4 sixes), caught by substitute Kumar Kushagra off part-timer Naman Dhir.

Auqib Nabi induced consecutive edges from Will Young while on 5, only for Rohit Sharma to shell a straightforward chance at first slip and keeper Ishan Kishan to drop a diving effort to his right on the very next delivery.

Tim Seifert punished the Indian attack, reaching his half-century off just 39 deliveries (5 fours, 3 sixes).

#2737. Marcus Smart suspended for throwing punch that made contact with Warriors player's face

Houston Rockets guard Marcus Smart has been suspended for "throwing a punch that made contact with the face" of opponent Charles Bassey during Wednesday's game against the Golden State Warriors.

The NBA released a statement on Thursday, Nov. 12 announcing the Rockets guard is being suspended three games without pay for the incident.

The night before, Smart grazed the face of Bassey when he threw a punch with 21 seconds left in the third quarter after the whistle was blown for a separate foul. Their arms had been caught in each other during a play and, when game play was stopped, Smart seemingly snapped.

After the punch was thrown, players from both teams got in a scuffle and, as the scene was broken up, the 2021-22 Defensive Player of the Year started walking to the locker room. It seemed as if he was sure he would be given a flagrant foul 2 and ejected from the game, which, after a review, he was.

Just before the incident, Smart and Bassey got tangled up under the rim when trying to box out during a Warriors possession. The two continued to jaw at each other up the floor. Then, when play halted, Smart squared up and threw a right-handed hook that nearly landed on Bassey's cheek. Bassey had moved his head backward to avoid contact. Officials later said that Smart made contact to Bassey's nose.

After the game, which the Rockets won 115-108, Bassey criticized Smart for his "fake toughness."

Houston head coach Ime Udoka also addressed the incident and shared Smart's side of the story.

"Marcus, I just talked to him, he said they got wrapped up and his elbow that he had hurt got bent up," the coach said. "And so he said something to him and Bassey said, 'What you going to do?' and he did it."

The former Oklahoma State standout will miss the Rockets' next three games due to his suspension. Houston faces the Utah Jazz, Washington Wizards and Miami Heat.

Smart's suspension will be lifted to play in the road game against the Indiana Pacers on Wednesday, Nov. 18.

Smart is averaging 8.3 points, 2.6 rebounds, 2 assists and a steal per game this season, his first with the Rockets.

He had six points, two rebounds and an assist before being booted from the Warriors matchup.

LaMelo Ball was once again the star of the show for the Minnesota Timberwolves as they beat the Dallas Mavericks 133-94.

The Wolves have now won five games in a row, and the latest one against the Mavs was their most dominant victory yet.

What the T-Wolves superstar is also being hailed for is the way he got the better of Cooper Flagg when they faced each other in one-on-one situations.

The NBA's official X account posted a small compilation of Ball getting the better of Flagg during the Minnesota Timberwolves' win over the Dallas Mavericks.

The video showed three instances where Ball got the better of the Mavs star, so much so that the NBA captioned their tweet: "LaMelo frying Cooper Flagg."

Unsurprisingly, that has sparked a reaction on social media, with some claiming that Ball embarrassed Flagg, while others believe it was just good play all-round, with the former coming out on top.

Another wrote: "Not going to lie, he is, but these are all tough shots. So Cooper ain't doing too bad."

Another fan reacted by saying: "Looked like pretty decent defence with an incredible finish from Melo."

"LaMelo Ball cooks Cooper Flagg," wrote another.

Flagg's defending wasn't awful by any means, but he will be the first to admit that he could've done better to stop Ball.

#2733. FCS Week 11 Game of the Week: Mercer Bears @ Tennessee Tech Golden Eagles: How to Watch, Preview, Predictions

The de facto SoCon championship will take place on Saturday afternoon in Cookeville with Tennessee Tech (9-1, 6-1 SoCon) hosting Mercer (8-2, 5-1 SoCon). The #9 Golden Eagles are looking to win the conference in their first year in it but standing the way is the Bears squad that's taken it the last two seasons. The two newfound league mates both were in the playoffs a year ago but both got bounced right away. They've each used their early exits to fuel what has been a terrific run in 2026 up to this point.

TTU likes to let it rip a score a lot of points. Mercer is more than happy getting into a low-scoring dogfight (as was evident by last week's 14-7 overtime win over Chattanooga). Which of these clashing styles will prove to be the winning formula this weekend? Whoever has it may not only be in line for a league title but also a top eight playoff seed in a few weeks.

Mercer has not seen a drop off in success even through the coaching transition into the Joel Taylor era. Taylor is in his first season in Macon, at least as the head coach, after a great year leading West Georgia to an 8-3 run last fall. Taylor spent two years with the Wolves going 12-10 in that span. But he has also been with the Bears before as well, serving as the team's defensive coordinator from 2020 to 2023. Now back in Macon, he's already a frontrunner for SoCon Coach of the Year and is one win away from tying the team's total from last year. Taylor is a South Carolina State alum and former defensive back.

Bobby Wilder, meanwhile, is in his third season in charge of the Golden Eagles and the turnaround has been an impressive one. Wilder, who was Old Dominion's head man for 11 years, has completely overhauled the Tennessee Tech program and turned them into a contender. Last year was a watershed moment as he got them back to the playoffs for only the second time in school history. Wilder's team went 11-2 last fall and is on pace to at least match that mark again.

Mercer has had some trouble figuring out who their main quarterback is this year but lately it's been junior J.P. Pickles. Pickles has thrown for 10 touchdowns this year and just two interceptions. Where's been quiet in passing, though, he's more than made up for with his running ability. Pickles has nearly 600 yards on the ground with another nine TDs with his legs. The Bears rely heavily on that rushing attack and he's a big part of it.

Also a big component of the ground game are running backs Zahmari Palode-Gary and Devon Caldwell. The standout senior Palode-Gary leads the team with 623 yards and averages 6.6 per tote while Caldwell checks in with 574 yards and a 6.2-yard-per-carry average. Those two will see a lot of the tough work up the gut and they'll have a tall task against a Tennessee Tech defense that is allowing 155.2 rushing yards per game right now.

The biggest threat to Mercer's ball carriers on Saturday will surely be senior defensive lineman Hudson Tucker. Tucker is the game-wrecker up front for the Golden Eagles with six sacks and eight tackles for loss (team highs in both). His ability to bully his way through the offensive line is excellent but he also won't be the only one that the Bears' backfield will have to be concerned with. Ameer Johnson and Tyrese Whitaker are also very sound in the trenches.

Tennessee Tech's linebacking corps is stout as well. Greg Turner III and Kaleb Brown head up the group and have been a formidable duo over the middle for opposing offenses this year. The pair has combined for 126 total tackles, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery. It will be strength-on-strength when Mercer opts to run the ball. And that might be exactly why they'll need to tap into their passing game which has, at times, gone dormant this season.

Fortunately for the Bears, receiver Brayden Smith will be on the outside. Smith has been the bright spot for the aerial attack, hauling in 51 passes for 734 yards and six scores. He could have a big day if the the Golden Eagles are too focused on stopping the run. It's not unheard of for TTU's defense to give up some big passing numbers either. If Pickles can get some time to sling it to Smith, Mercer might be in business.

This game will really be won or lost on the matchup between the high-scoring Golden Eagles offense and the stifling Mercer defense and Tennessee Tech has to like their chances with quarterback Jax Leatherwood under center. Leatherwood has been terrific this season, throwing for 2,629 yards and 26 touchdowns along with just four interceptions. He'll let the ball rip but also takes good care of it. That, however, will be tested against a defense that ranks near the top of the FCS in picks.

Mercer has intercepted 12 passes this year and the majority of those have come from their talented secondary. That secondary is composed of some truly special corners, the best perhaps being senior Cameron Goggins. Goggins leads the team with five picks on his own and six pass breakups. Behind him are Justin Ferguson (three interceptions) and Evin McDowell (two interceptions). Leatherwood will have danger all around him when he throws in this one.

He will also have some lethal receivers, though. Tre' Holloway, Gabe Nunez and Eric Weatherly are as deadly of a receiving trio as the Bears will see all season. Holloway has 656 yards, Nunez has 599 and Weatherly has 518. Between them there are 17 touchdowns through the air. Leatherwood will have his pick of the litter every time he wants to throw.

That being said, Tennessee Tech simply cannot pass all game without it coming back to bite them against those cornerbacks. That means that running backs M.J. Flowers and Qua Ashley will need to relieve some of the pressure off the pass game. Flowers is the team's leading rusher with 655 yards and seven touchdowns while Ashley has 357 yards and five scores. Those two may end up being the X factors if the Golden Eagles are able to win.

The Bears will look to slow them down with stud linebacker Jyarius Carter. Carter has 86 tackles this year as well as 2.5 sacks and an interception. He's done a little bit of everything for the Mercer D that gives up just 16.3 points per game. He and fellow linebacker Ronin Dangler will be flying around at the heart of the defense. Dangler is also the team leader with 5.5 sacks.

Mercer will simply not be able to completely stop Tennessee Tech's offense from making big plays. The key for them will be to mitigate the damage. Even if they do slow down the Golden Eagles, though, there are serious questions about their own offense being able to make enough plays to stay in it. TTU has not scored under 20 points once this year. The Bears have done it four times. There will be a ton of pressure on the Mercer defense to make this a slugfest because they are not built to win a track meet style game that Tennessee Tech will want to play. The Golden Eagles will have more trouble with this Mercer defense than most they've seen this year but Leatherwood and the offense have too many weapons at their disposal. Try as they might, the Bears just won't be able to keep pace.

Score Prediction: Tennessee Tech: 34 – Mercer: 20

#2732. Alexander Ovechkin announces this will be his last NHL season: 'Let's have fun'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

#2729. Sixers take care of business without LeBron, secure 10th vs. Raptors

Maybe not the blowout people are looking for, but still a pretty decent win. The Sixers erased a 17-point first half deficit to defeat the Toronto Raptors 123-112 Thursday night.

Tyrese Maxey led the Sixers with 27 shooting 8-of-13 from the field along with eight assists. Joel Embiid didn't quite break out of his shooting slump, but looked much better as he avoided an injury scare early in the game. He finished with 20 points going 7-of-17 from the floor along with four rebounds.

Jaylen Brown had an up-and-down night, going 8-of-15 from the field for 18 points and six rebounds. VJ Edgecombe had another great swiss army knife game, finishing with 15 points, eight rebounds and eight assists. R.J. Barrett led all scorers with 31.

LeBron James was out for this one with lower back management, as well as Adem Bona (neck) and Dominick Barlow (back). Toronto was without Kawhi Leonard, Scottie Barnes, and Trayce Jackson-Davis.

The Sixers opened the game generating good shots. Brown shook free of CMB for a pull-up jumper, Dean Wade and Edgecombe both stepped into open threes, and Embiid got a jumper from the free throw line, but none of these looks fell. Maxey finally got the Sixers their first field goal of the game getting the ball off a broken play and getting to the basket.

Embiid set a screen for Maxey to help him get open on the three-point line and appeared to bang knees with Ja'Kobe Walter as Walter was trying to fight through the screen. Embiid went down in a heap of pain immediately and the Sixers stopped the game so he could head back to the locker room.

The Sixers' offense continued to struggle after the stoppage. Brown was trying attack off the dribble but was getting bottled up. They still couldn't hit a three off the catch either — the rest of the team started the game 0-of-4 from deep. The Raptors ripped off a 12-0 run during this stretch.

For the second game in a row, Edgecombe had a really nice spin move to split defenders and get to the basket. Darko Rajakovich called timeout after he did so, which allowed Embiid to emerge from the locker room and return to the game. Edgecombe did just about the same thing coming out of the timeout.

Maxey ran quick off a miss to create a fast break layup, but Toronto was able to snuff out the momentum quickly. The Sixers went into a zone for a couple of possessions, but the Raptors shooters had gotten into a rhythm and they were able to get open pretty easily. Two threes from Barrett and another from Jamison Battle helped them score 13 more unanswered points.

Embiid nearly passed up a wide open layup near the basket, but did eventually put it up once he realized the 6-foot-1 Jamal Shead was guarding him for his first field goal of the game. Maxey was able to hit a ridiculous layup in transition, and Anfernee Simons drilled a three at the buzzer to pull the Sixers to within nine.

Simons drilled a stepback three with a hand in his face to open the quarter. Embiid, looking a bit more comfortable, blocked a layup and got himself an easy bucket going to the paint. Brown wasn't able to bury his three after making Kyle Anderson fall with a crossover, but he finally got a midrange to go that capped off a 15-0 Sixers run going back to the first.

That seemed to do the trick as Brown drilled his next two pull-ups in the midrange. Edgecombe was the best Sixer on the floor for much of the first half. His intercepting of passes from the weak side was the best defense they had going for them, and it was creating plenty of transition opportunities. On top of a big fast break dunk, Edgecombe also hit a very nifty up-and-under layup.

It probably gave everyone a good scare, but Embiid was able to get by Jakob Poeltl and throw down a dunk, albeit one that did not look like the smoothest landing. The Sixers' offense started scorching, but a lack of stops prevented them from building a lead. Nick Nurse called a timeout to regroup after they allowed two offensive rebounds on one possession, ending with a putback.

That timeout also gave Nurse a chance to put Maxey back in the game, who immediately went straight to the basket and got fouled. After teams traded threes, Maxey got to the hoop again, but Embiid picked up his third foul of the night trying to grab a defensive rebound and had to sit for the last two and a half minutes of the half.

Brown took up the mantle offensively, nailing another pull-up and driving for a layup. Jabari Walker, who didn't have much of an impact in his first shift, picked up an offensive rebound and drew a foul pulling down another. His putback was answered with another three from Barrett. Wade missed another open three on the ensuing possession, keeping the game tied at 60 at the break.

Both teams stayed hot coming out of the break as Wade and Edgecombe each drilled a corner three. On the other end of the floor the Raptors drove right to the basket for three easy layups. Immanuel Quickley also drilled a very deep, very contested pull-up three. Embiid missed a fadeaway over Poeltl, but got himself another easy dunk playing high-low with Edgecombe.

The Sixers were still giving up plenty of easy baskets off simple actions, but they were guarding one-on-one better when the Raptors isolated. Brown blocked a Barrett layup and jumped a passing lane for a pick-six. Screens ended up being risky plays on the night as Kentavious Caldwell-Pope came up favoring his shoulder trying to fight through one, but he didn't have to leave the game.

Despite throwing a post-entry pass for Brown a little too far, Embiid seemed to finding his comfort offensively. He was confident in his physical advantages over Poeltl and was aggressive because of that. It did seem like he was trying to dunk as much as he could, which did lead to him fumbling away an attempt at the basket.

Embiid is still waiting on that midrange game to come back around as he was long on another free throw line jumper. It remained a hot Simons game, something the team desperately needed with how they've been shooting lately.

Maxey was a consistent source of scoring to close the quarter, but stops on the other end continued to come at a premium. The Sixers were finally able to get some space after Quickley missed a pretty open layup after beating Maxey through the paint. Simons got it up the floor for a transition basket. The Raptors called a timeout to regroup, but CMB got called for a moving screen on the first play coming out of it. Maxey got to the line, which Barrett responded to by backing him down in the post for a layup, bringing the Sixers lead back down to nine after three.

Walker opened the quarter with a corner three and just missed a second a few possessions later. He did scoop up another putback after Edgecombe's attempt to dunk on two Raptors came up empty, and Simons swiped the ball away from Barrett for a fast break bucket to start the quarter strong.

At some point in the first half, the ball got stuck behind the backboard and the crowd let Poeltl hear it as he struggled to knock it free with a broom. When the ball got stuck again in the fourth, a referee brought the broom back to Poeltl on the bench for a chance at redemption. The crowd got a kick out of it, but Poeltl did not, and refused. The crowd shared a sarcastic celebration with KCP after it took him a few attempts to dislodge it.

The Sixers' offense seemed to hit a bit of a lull midway through the fourth. Brown missed a pair of free throws and was blocked again at the rim by CMB. Edgecombe tried to hit Brown with a lob but that was broken up by CMB again, but Edgecombe was able to pick it back up and finish it himself. After giving up second chance points on the following possession, Nurse called a timeout to put Embiid and Maxey back in the game.

The Raptors got another basket inside, a trip to the line, and a corner three to cut the lead down to six with plenty of time left. Simons hit a much needed three, as was the case for much of the night. Embiid finally knocked down a midrange after a couple of stops, but Quickley walked into an open three off a screen on the next trip down the floor.

Maxey got to the line again as the Raptors started to run out of time. Embiid got past a couple of defenders and nearly had another self lob off the backboard, but that was also broken up by CMB. Embiid was still able to secure the ball and get it to KCP, who buried a three right before the shot clock expired. Embiid hit a midrange on the following possession, wrapping up this game quite nicely for both himself and the team.

The double-digit lead gave the fans enough confidence for loud "We Want Tacko" chants, and Nurse obliged, putting Tacko Fall in for the final 54 seconds of the game. Poor Jabari Walker got a round of boos when he went to the scorer's table on account of not being Tacko Fall.

#2728. Instant analysis of the Commanders' win against the New York Giants

The Washington Commanders took down the New York Giants 24-21 in their ninth game of the season at MetLife Stadium. It was their second straight division win, improving their record to 3-5-1, putting them just two games behind the Giants and giving them the tiebreaker.

This started out as a defense-dominated game with a score of 10-7 at halftime. Washington scored first with a field goal following an 11-play drive in the second quarter. However, the Giants had the first touchdown on a 16-play, 72-yard drive that took nearly eight minutes. The Commanders responded with a touchdown of their own just before halftime when quarterback Jayden Daniels connected with Ben Sinnott for his first touchdown of the season on third-and-goal.

Washington started the second half with a three-and-out, while the Giants were able to get a touchdown on their first drive of the second half, giving them a 14-10 lead. Again, the Commanders came right back with a touchdown of their own to regain the lead. On New York's subsequent drive, the defense forced a fumble from wide receiver Malik Nabers for the game's first turnover. Washington took a 17-14 lead into the fourth quarter.

Things fell apart for the Commanders a bit in the fourth quarter. Their first three drives of the quarter ended in a turnover on downs and two interceptions from Daniels. New York was not able to capitalize on either of the picks, but they did score a touchdown after the turnover on downs to give the Giants a 21-17 lead.

With their season on the line, Washington got the ball back with 1:46 left in the game. They had decent field position at New York's 29-yard line after the Giants had a 14-yard punt. Wide receiver Treylon Burks was able to draw a 33-yard pass interference penalty to get the Commanders inside Giants territory. Three plays later, Daniels connected with Stefon Diggs for a 32-yard touchdown to give Washington a 24-21 lead with under a minute left in the game.

New York had one final chance to send this game to overtime or win the game. They had all three timeouts to work with and got inside of Washington territory. However, on third and 10, Giants' quarterback J.J. McCarthy tried to force it downfield and the Commanders made him pay with an interception from Rasul Douglas to seal the 24-21 victory.

When he caught the ball, it initially looked like he would be tackled shortly after picking up the first down. However, as soon as he broke away from the Giants' defenders, no one was left to stop him, and he easily scored. This touchdown kept Washington's season alive, as a loss in this game would have essentially doomed their season.

7/14: Throughout the first eight games of the season, the Washington Commanders have struggled to convert on third down. However, that was not a problem in this game. In fact, their ability to convert 50 percent of their third-down attempts in this game was a weapon against the Giants. If they can keep up this third-down efficiency, the Commanders could realistically find themselves in the playoffs.

2: Each team had two turnovers in this game. New York was not able to capitalize on Washington's turnovers, but the takeaways proved to be critical in this game for the Commanders. The first takeaway stopped the Giants from potentially scoring and the second takeaway sealed the game for Washington. Their defense needed to get some takeaways in this game for the Commanders to win and that is exactly what they did.

4: Washington has struggled with penalties all season. However, in this game, they had a season-low four penalties for just 17 yards. Finally, the Commanders were able to go a whole 60 minutes without shooting themselves in the foot with unnecessary penalties. This is what winning football looks like and if Washington can play like this more, they could string together some wins.

QB Jayden Daniels: This has not been a great season for Daniels, who had yet to throw for more than two touchdowns in a game and missed time with his elbow injury. He also had two interceptions in the fourth quarter, which could have been costly for Washington. However, he bounced back on the final drive to lead the Commanders to their third victory of the season and keep their playoff chances alive.

TE Ben Sinnott: When Chig Okonkwo had to exit with an injury, Ben Sinnott stepped up and played well for Washington's offense. His hurdle may have been one of the most impressive of the season, and his touchdown was impressive, too. Maybe he will get more offensive snaps in the second half of the season.

CB Rasul Douglas: Defensively, the Commanders needed takeaways if they were going to win this game. With a different corner in coverage, McCarthy's shot downfield easily could have been completed to give the Giants a chance to win with a touchdown or force overtime with a field goal. However, Douglas had perfect coverage on the play and after dropping an earlier touchdown, he sealed the victory for the Commanders.

After defeating the Giants and getting within two games in the NFC East race, the Washington Commanders now have a mini-bye ahead of their game against the Cincinnati Bengals on Monday Night Football. The Commanders will be looking to win back-to-back games for the first time this season.

#2727. 'Who let the dogs out?' Jameis Winston busts out hilarious cadence

Leave it to Jameis Winston to allow Thursday night's game to go to the dogs.

The New York Giants veteran backup quarterback, who now doubles as something of a short-yardage specialist, tried to draw the Washington Commanders offside with 3:27 remaining in the game when the NFC East-leading Giants faced a fourth-and-1 from their own 11-yard line while nursing a 21-17 lead.

Lined up in a bunched formation, Winston began yelling out signals, but Washington held its ground. When that didn't work, the No. 1 pick of the 2015 NFL Draft reset the formation and invoked the Baha Men with this cadence: "Who let the dogs out? Who, who, who, who, who?" ... the latter portion naturally sounding like barking.

But the Commanders didn't bite, and the Giants had to punt.

Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels threw a seemingly crucial interception four plays later, but the Giants went three-and-out on the subsequent drive. That punt proved costly as the Commanders scored what turned out to be the winning touchdown on the ensuing drive of what turned out to be a 24-21 triumph, one that likely saved their season.

Winston converted a 1-yard sneak on fourth down in the second quarter for a first down but couldn't do the same on the play prior to his cadence hijinks − the 1-yard run and first down he originally seemed to manage overturned after Washington challenged the spot. He has rushed 20 times this season for a meager 62 yards but has picked up 12 first downs.

Following the loss, Giants coach John Harbaugh said his team had "seven dogfights" left as the regular season continues to run its course. Whether Big Blue successfully lets the dogs out in any of those matchups remains to be seen.

#2724. John Harbaugh expresses confidence in K Dominic Zvada

Giants rookie kicker Dominic Zvada has missed six field goals in nine games. He missed another on Thursday night, a 33-yarder.

While it happened in the first quarter and not on the final play, it stands out in a game that was decided by three points.

After New York's 24-21 loss to the Commanders, Giants coach John Harbaugh was asked about his level of confidence in Zvada.

"Yeah, we're confident," Harbaugh said. "You know, you can't — as soon as a guy doesn't make a play, I mean, start firing people left and right. Especially your kicker who's a rookie. So I'm confident that he's gonna become a good kicker. I mean, if at some point in time, it doesn't happen, it doesn't happen.

"But I'm not gonna panic, you know, halfway through the season when the guy who's made a bunch of kicks, if that's what you're inferring we should be doing.  So, you know, I mean, we're just not gonna knee-jerk it like that. He's gonna make kicks. He's gonna make a lot of kicks, I believe in him.  I think he's really good, really talented. And we're gonna give him an opportunity to do it. It's up to him to do it."

That's a fair assessment of a player who's still new to the NFL. But a kicker has one job. If he can't do it (especially from distances that should be automatic), at some point tough questions need to be asked.

Basically, how much time will Zvada get before Harbaugh decides it's not going to happen? That remains to be seen, if Zvada keeps missing kicks he should be making.

#2722. Justin Jefferson: It's a joy to see Kirk Cousins take over as a leader

Kirk Cousins is back in Minnesota, and perhaps no one is more excited about that than Justin Jefferson.

The wide receiver had career highs in catches (128) and yards (1,809) and earned the NFL’s Offensive Player of the Year award in Cousins’ last full season with the Vikings in 2022.

Jefferson, though, said he has “no expectations.”

“It’s really just going out there and just executing our plays,” Jefferson said, via Kevin Seifert of ESPN. “It’s not really getting too juiced up about him being here or anybody being back there. It’s just all about understanding the plays that are being called, understanding the jobs that we have and executing our responsibilities. And just the plays that are there, and the plays that could be made, we just need to continue to just make those type of plays. And I’m pretty sure that the results would be a lot better.

“He just understands the game. He’s a guy that studies the game a lot. He understands how the defenses play, especially covering me. And he understands, the plays that we have called that are kind of my plays and he understands the timing and the windows to throw those type of plays, but he also doesn’t force those type of plays to me and he just lets the game come to me.”

Jefferson said it was “a joy to hear [Cousins] just take over and be a leader in the meeting room, on the field.”

“He’s being vocal,” Jefferson said. “Just making sure that everybody hears the plays that he’s talking about and the notes that he has for certain routes, certain plays. And he’s just making sure that everybody’s on the same page. So it’s definitely cool to hear that type of leadership and command. If you know Kirk, that’s pretty normal from him. So it’s definitely kind of cool him being back in that room and him taking that control.”

#2720. Commanders help Cowboys’ NFC East hopes with TNF win over Giants

The NFC East just became a tiny bit easier for the Dallas Cowboys. They owe the Washington Commanders big time.

For what it's worth, the Commanders (3-5-1) are also now a factor. Their remaining schedule could see them find a way, too.

#2719. Toronto falls to stacked Sixers’ offence

The Toronto Raptors continued a challenging stretch of their schedule tonight, facing the Philadelphia 76ers on the second night of a back-to-back, this time on the road. After coming apart at the seams despite an early lead against Boston, the Raptors' intention to move on was thwarted by a Sixers team that handed the Raptors a similar loss. A significant early lead dwindled by the half, ultimately leading to Toronto falling, this time 112 to 123.

To no surprise, Philly's big names of Joel Embiid (20 points), Jaylen Brown (18 points), VJ Edgecombe (15 points), and TJ Maxey (27 points) carried the Sixers. Anfernee Simons was their most productive bench player, offering clutch long-range shooting that gave the rest of the team space to operate, finishing with 17 points in the process.

Toronto saw excellent performances from RJ Barrett who finished with 31 points, 14 rebounds, and 5 assists, Immanuel Quickley who had 26 points, 4 rebounds, and 6 assists, and Collin Murray-Boyles chipping in 14 points, 4 assists, and 5 blocks.

The Raptors had their hands full early, needing to answer for a number of offensive weapons on a Sixers team that is building plenty of hype for a championship contender. They didn't need to face LeBron James who sat due to sciatica, but the remaining four of their starters remained a formidable challenge.

Toronto targeted Embiid early, forcing him into awkward defensive coverages that required speed and lateral movement that he struggled with as a result of his laundry list of injuries. After knee-to-knee contact, Embiid briefly visited the locker room but returned a few minutes later.

RJ and Quickley were quick to answer their less-than-savory performances last night. Quickley worked hard to distribute the ball and get everyone going early while RJ hit a pair of threes on consecutive possessions.

Just like last night, their offense was running smoothly. They built a significant 33-16 lead, and it felt like everything was going in the Raptors' favour until in the final two minutes of the frame, the tide slowly started to turn. Philly went on an unanswered 8-point run to close the quarter.

In the second quarter, the Sixers were able to close the gap and draw ahead, making much of the second frame a back-and-forth contest.

Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Anfernee Simons showed their abilities from beyond the arc, creating spacing for the Sixers' starters to operate in the paint where they're comfortable. Tyrese Maxey was almost unstoppable from virtually everywhere on the floor. Jaylen Brown started to come alive as well, an equally challenging offensive player to find an answer for.

Toronto had contributions from everyone, with CMB, Barrett, Martin, and Battle all making long range shots. Their ball movement helped limit poor shot selection, and even when they were missing shots, Walter stood out as having a motor, with a phenomenal put-back that showed the Raptors were going to fight through the fatigue. By the end of the half, the game was all tied up.

The third quarter mirrored the second, going blow-for-blow with Philly. Ties and lead changes riddled the period, with neither team able to build any kind of momentum or separation.

Alijah Martin has impressed with his continued active defence and fearless scoring, willing to take the ball through anyone. At times, the minutes with mostly bench players on the floor actually felt more cohesive and productive than without.

Despite best efforts, Philly's top four firepower was hard to contend with. Late in the third, a series of costly turnovers allowed the Sixers to get out in transition, managing a 8-0 run to build their largest lead, a 9-point advantage before the final twelve minutes of play.

Toronto's fatigue might have played a role as this game started to get away from them. Second effort isn't enough when you're struggling to make second and third shots, and despite their effort, a lot of them rolled off the rim and couldn't be recovered. Murray-Boyles' effort, however, should be celebrated. On one end, he was blocking shots and playing tough defence, and on the other, good screening and off-ball movement helped him be a standout on the court.

In the end, it wasn't enough to overcome Philly, and Toronto continues to seek their first win against a team over 0.500. Next, they'll face New York twice, with the first of the matchups on Sunday at 6 pm.

#2718. Giants QB Jameis Winston tries to fool Commanders with hilarious ‘who let the dogs out?’ snap count

Giants QB Jameis Winston tries to fool Commanders with hilarious 'who let the dogs out?' snap count appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Jameis Winston kept one crucial drive alive against the Washington Commanders. But then he turned to a unique snap count tactic for the New York Giants in the fourth quarter. He channeled "Baha Men" for this one despite losing 24-21 on Thursday Night Football.

Winston this time tried getting Washington to jump offsides in this fourth down situation. But instead of going with the normal "hut hut" call, he's overheard saying "Who let the dogs out?"

Washington never crossed the line of scrimmage. But still, the moment rose as a new zany tactic from Winston. And he drew some notable viral reactions.

"Jameis may have just put together the greatest snap count ever. Can't believe that didn't work," posted NBC Sports personality Jac Collinsworth on the social media website X, formerly Twitter.

"Never change, Jameis Winston," The Athletic posted in response to the clip.

"Straight comedy," added the NFL on ESPN account.

Once again, Winston never got the better end of the unique snap count. But he managed to trend online, plus get fans thinking about the famed hit song from the early 2000s.

Baha Men became popular in 2000 with the popular club hit song. But "Who Let The Dogs Out" grew into a stadium anthem. Schools like Mississippi State in the SEC started playing the track as a hype song before games. Ultimately, players in the huddle starting saying the five words to hype each other up.

Now Winston re-popularized Baha Men's only hit song. And rose as a highlight despite the Giants falling to Washington.

I hate to get so negative just one week into the season, but the Philadelphia Flyers have forced my hand. After a magical run to the second round of the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs, the Flyers have fallen on their face through four games.

There's still plenty of time -- 80 games exactly -- for the Flyers to get back on track and restore that optimism, but to say this has been a discouraging start would be an understatement.

#2715. Aaron Donald on having no sacks: "They come in bunches"

Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald has played seven games this season. He has no sacks.

“Sacks come in bunches,” Donald told reporters on Thursday. “It’s going to come. Just keep playing ball and keep finding ways to win. That’s the most important thing is winning. No pressure, I’m not worried about it. I’ve been playing football since I was five, six years old. They come in bunches. They’ll come eventually so just keep doing what I need to do to help this team. When they present themselves, hopefully hold the ball and take advantage of it.”

On Sunday, Donald finally played with Myles Garrett, the player whose arrival in June sparked Donald’s decision to return after two years of retirement. Garrett, in his first game since Week 1, had 3.0 sacks and a forced fumble.

Regardless, the Rams won, pushing themselves above .500 for the first time this year. On Sunday at Arizona, they have a chance to win their fourth in a row.

And Donald has another chance to get his first sack since he returned from retirement.

#2712. Cade Cunningham has historic night as Pistons outlast Wizards in bloody battle

AJ Dybantsa collided with Cade Cunningham during the Washington Wizards' game against the Detroit Pistons on Thursday, Nov. 12 and was bloodied on the play.

Dybantsa didn't miss any action and even sent the game into its second overtime, but Cunningham ended up being the star of the game. The Pistons guard scored a career-high 52 points at Capital One Arena to dismantle the Wizards 144-140 in double overtime. He added 11 assists, five rebounds, a steal and a block. He did not commit a turnover.

According to the league, he is the first player ever to notch at least 50 points and 10 assists in a game without turning the ball over.

The 2021 No. 1 overall pick passed his previous career high when he scored his 47th point in the first overtime with a 3-point bucket that tied the game at 130.

As for the collision, with 26 seconds left in regulation and the Wizards up 118-117, Cunningham was dribbling the ball and attempted to twirl and switch directions. The Wizards rookie and 2026 No. 1 overall pick was guarding him and, when Cunningham spun back around, his jaw smacked into the side of Dybantsa's face.

Dybantsa fell backwards onto the court and grabbed his mouth as he laid on his back. Blood started dripping from his mouth. A trainer tended to him as he continued lying on the hardwood.

The game went into overtime with the score tied at 121 at the end of the fourth quarter. Dybantsa sent the game to a second overtime, seemingly no worse for wear. He took a pass from Trae Young, dribbled and took a jump shot at the charity stripe to tie the game at 132 with 0.1 second left.

The rookie finished with five points, eight rebounds and four assists for the Wizards.

Washington was led by Young, who had 37 points and 14 assists. Anthony Davis notched a double-double of his own with 30 points and 15 boards. Alex Sarr added 30 points and nine rebounds.

#2711. Thursday Night Football: Stefon Diggs' late TD gives Commanders 24-21 win

With 3:27 remaining in Thursday’s game, the Giants lined up with Jameis Winston under center on fourth-and-1 from their own 11. The team’s backup quarterback, who runs the team’s quarterback sneaks, yelled, “Hut One. Hut Two. Hut Three. Who let the dogs out? Who, who, who, who?”

The Giants took a delay of game and then punted.

The Commanders got the last laugh, winning 24-21 on Stefon Diggs’ 32-yard touchdown with 57 seconds left. The Commanders are 3-5-1 and the Giants 5-3-1.

In an entertaining second half, the teams traded the lead four times.

The Giants took a 21-17 lead with 8:13 left on Isaiah Likely’s 66-yard catch-and-run.

The Giants then had back-to-back interceptions of Jayden Daniels. Safety Jevon Holland, who is having an All-Pro season, took the ball away from Chig Okonkwo at the 2-yard line with the Commanders on the Giants 24 with 5:27 left, and Ar’Darius Washington stepped in front of Okonkwo on fourth-and-2 at the Washington 45 with 2:15 left.

The Giants, though, couldn’t run out the clock, and the Commanders made the most of it. They needed only three plays to go 71 yards thanks to a questionable 33-yard pass interference penalty on Deonte Banks, who was covering Treylon Burks. Three plays later, Diggs scored.

The Giants reached the Washington 48 on their final drive, but J.J. McCarthy’s deep throw to Malik Nabers was intercepted by Rasul Douglas with 25 seconds left to end it.

The Giants outgained the Commanders 399 to 340, but missed a field goal and had two turnovers.

Daniels was 23-of-33 for 249 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions. Rachaad White ran for 47 yards on 11 carries, and Diggs caught six passes for 83 yards. Antonio Williams and Ben Sinnott each caught a touchdown pass.

McCarthy was 23-of-36 for 293 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Cam Skattebo had 18 carries for 78 yards and two touchdowns and caught three passes for 44 yards, and Likely had nine receptions for 127 yards and a touchdown.

The NHL is not what it is today without Ovechkin and Crosby, and they entered the league together in 2005. They have faced off 100 times in the NHL, including 25 games in the playoffs. In those 100, they have combined for 231 points. A total of 90 games saw either find the score sheet and 49 had both record a point in the same game.

They have met in four postseason series, each in the second round. Crosby and the Penguins won the first three series and won the Cup each time. The Capitals won in 2018 and won their first and still only Stanley Cup. They have played 75 regular-season games in the series. Crosby leads 43-28-4 and has 35 goals and 62 assists in those. Ovechkin has 38 goals and 33 helpers.

The 39-year-old Crosby is in the final year of his contract but has said he has no plans to retire. He and Ovechkin have joined Howe, Alex Delvecchio, Stan Mikita and Steve Yzerman as the only players in NHL history to play 22 seasons with one franchise.

"Over the years, obviously, I've developed a friendship with him and have a ton of respect for him," Crosby said to the media Monday with the Ovechkin news. "It's tough, you come into the league at 18 years old, and before we even met, we were built up against each other."

It should be Logan Thompson in net for Washington, and he was excellent in his season debut in allowing two goals in a win at defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina last Friday. Last season at home, he was 19-9-5 with a 2.18 GAA and three shutouts. Thompson made two starts vs. Pittsburgh overall last campaign and won both with a 1.50 GAA.

The Penguins and Capitals have three meetings left, including Washington's home finale on April 4. That should be quite the Sunday night if both Crosby and Ovechkin are healthy then. Tickets on the secondary market are north of $800 to get in.

#2709. Holy Trinity dominates Foundation Academy in regional quarterfinal

MELBOURNE — Holy Trinity played its first FHSAA state playoff game in two years, returning after one SSAA season to compete in the newly created Independent League.

The top-seeded Tigers hosted No. 8 seed Foundation Academy in the Pool B South regional quarterfinals looking to win their first postseason game in five years.

After they built a 17-6 halftime lead, Holy Trinity dominated the second half to win 45-6 for the school's fourth-ever state playoff win.

"I thought the kids came out and played great. Defensively, we were just flying to the football making some pretty good plays," Holy Trinity head coach Hurlie Brown said. "We stumbled a little bit, but it never affected the team. We just kept playing. That's what you ask for. Just go out and play for 48 minutes. That's what they did."

The Tigers defense held an opponent to under 10 points for the sixth time in 10 games this season. They forced Foundation Academy into six punts and two interceptions. Foundation Academy ended the game with 145 total yards with its lone touchdown coming off a muffed punt.

"I got a really good defense. That's what's expected of them. I don't expect anything different," Brown said. "We let them get out of the pocket a little bit a couple times, but I thought they did exactly what we were asking them to do. They did a fantastic job."

Holy Trinity senior Omari Savage put the exclamation mark on the win with interceptions on back-to-back defensive snaps off Lions backup quarterback John Elder.

Savage picked off Elder with Foundation Academy driving in Tigers territory. The senior returned the interception 78 yards to the end zone.

On the next Lions drive, Savage intercepted a pass over the middle of the field and returned it 28 yards to the Foundation Academy 13-yard line. That set up the final score of the night on a 13-yard touchdown run by freshman Michael Jackson.

"It felt good," Savage said. "They finally threw the ball my way. I'm going to get it every time."

The defensive front of Holy Trinity was disruptive all night. Freshman Jadiel Corbin recorded a pair of sacks and sophomore Jacorey Mills brought down Foundation Academy starting quarterback Micah Brinkley for one sack.

"We just feel safe," Savage said. "We can just make sure we do our part and we know they're going to do theirs."

The Tigers offense squandered red zone chances on their first two drives as they had a field goal blocked followed by a 27-yard field goal by senior Roan Wright as time expired in the first quarter. However, they settled into the game and scored five touchdowns on their final seven possessions.

Holy Trinity sophomore Jackson Mobley completed 15-of-21 passes for 183 yards and three touchdowns. Mobley threw a 10-yard touchdown to junior Hayden Argo to make it 10-0 midway through the second quarter.

After a Foundation Academy touchdown with 49 seconds left in the first half, Mobley chucked a deep ball to junior Aaron Raines in the middle of the field. Raines hauled in the pass with one arm and shed a pair of Lions defensive backs for a 63-yard touchdown. The sophomore tossed a 20-yard touchdown pass to junior Zach Curran to make it 24-6 with 2:20 remaining in the third quarter.

Jackson and Mills combined for 141 rushing yards on 15 carries and two touchdowns. Mills broke the longest run of the game of 45 yards for a touchdown in the fourth quarter.

"I felt if we just kept playing, eventually it was going to come. That's just football. They had a great game plan for us. They executed well," Brown said. "We got a field goal blocked, but then we were able to get three points off the other one getting in the red zone. That's something now we got to go back and look at and get it corrected and make sure that we don't make those same mistakes again."

Holy Trinity features a very young team with just 10 seniors. Despite their inexperience, the Tigers went 7-2 in the regular season and controlled their first playoff game from start to finish.

"We've had some ups and downs, but we get through it every time. It's a real brotherhood here," Savage said. "Being here since my sophomore year and now being a senior, just seeing the culture change and all that. I just feel proud."

Holy Trinity returns to the field on Nov. 19 for the regional semifinals against the No. 5 seed Central Florida Christian Academy. CFCA defeated No. 4 seed Orangewood Christian 18-10 in its regional quarterfinal. The Tigers will look to make history and reach their first regional final.

"A win's a win," Savage said. "We just have to keep on going and just focus on the next one."

This article originally appeared on Florida Today: Holy Trinity dominates Foundation Academy in regional quarterfinal

#2707. Recap: Wizards down Pistons in 2OT, 144-140

The Washington Wizards' struggles continued Thursday night, as they fell to the Detroit Pistons 144-140 in double overtime (8-3) at Capital One Arena to extend their losing streak to six games.

Playing the second night of a back-to-back after a 114-101 loss to the Indiana Pacers on Wednesday, Washington (4-9) once again could not close out a close game in the fourth quarter, first or second overtime periods, which led to its second loss to the Pistons in the past four days after Monday night's 122-111 loss in Detroit.

Washington got out to an early 17-10 lead thanks to triples from Alex Sarr, Kyshawn George and Trae Young – which looked to be a positive sign from a team that entered the contest shooting 29.8% from distance.

Sarr started the game a perfect 4-for-4 from the field, quickly notching 10 points in the first quarter. His counterpart in the front court, Anthony Davis recorded 10 points on 5-of-7 shooting in first-quarter, to join Sarr in double-figure scoring.

However, in a lineup starring Trae Young, Tre Johnson, Bub Carrington, Bilal Coulibaly and Deandre Ayton, Washington's 10-point lead dissipated as the Pistons completed a 11-point swing to take a 33-32 lead over the Wizards to end the first quarter. After protecting the ball for the first nine minutes of the game, Washington coughed up four turnovers in the final 3:15 of the quarter to contribute to the Pistons run.

Washington steadied the ship before halftime with the help of Young, who scored eight second quarter points to help the Wizards stay within three and trail 64-61 entering the half. Davis paced Washington with 16 points and eight rebounds, while Sarr tacked on 14 points and Young scored 12. The trio combined for 69% of the Wizards first half points, and Sarr shot a perfect 6-for-6 from the field.

Rookie AJ Dybantsa appeared to truly struggle for the first time this season when matched up with Ausar Thompson. Dybantsa shot 0-of-2 from the field and looked uncomfortable with the ball in his hands when guarded by Thompson. Yet, the BYU product managed to record two assists and not turn the ball over in the first half, to finish with a team-high +11 when he was on the court.

After keeping the game close in the second quarter, Detroit erupted for an 11-point lead of its own with the help of Duncan Robinson who shot a perfect 3-for-3 from three point range during the run. Cade Cunningham also tacked on seven third quarter points to keep Washington at an arms length throughout the period.

The Wizards cut the lead back to four thanks to Alex Sarr, who remained perfect from the field, tacking on seven third quarter points to enter the fourth with 21 points and four rebounds. Tre Johnson was also in rhythm in the third, scoring six of his 13 points at the time while shooting 3-of-4 from the field.

Washington entered the fourth quarter trailing 94-90, with a chance to snap their five game skid in front of an energetic home crowd in D.C. — and Young matched the energy in Capital One Arena. He scored a quick nine points in the first four minutes of the fourth quarter to give Washington a 103-102, and found Coulibaly streaking down the court for an assist on a fast break.

But head coach Brian Keefe subbed Young out for a two-minute rest, and Detroit capitalized immediately with a 6-0 run to take a 108-103 lead. Washington kept it close, including taking a 118-117 lead with 31.5 seconds remaining thanks to a three from George. But Cunningham drew a foul from Dybantsa on the following possession, and knocked down two free throws to essentially seal the game. But 1.8 seconds remaining, Young buried a three at the buzzer to send the game to overtime, knotted at 121.

George knocked down a triple to give Washington a 124-121 lead in OT before picking up his sixth foul and being forced to sit the rest of the game. But in his absence, Young found Davis in the paint for a floater, and then drew a charge on the ensuing possession, which lead to Davis finding Sarr for the alley-oop to start overtime on a 7-0 run.

Detroit responded with a 6-0 run of its own led by Cunningham — who finished with a game-high 52 points and a team-high 11 assists. He sealed the game on back to back possessions, both in transition. First he nailed a triple to tie the game at 130, and then assisted Robinson on the break for a jumper to take a 132-130 lead with nine seconds remaining in the extra period.

Dybantsa, the rookie, took matters into his own hands and drove to the paint and pulled up for a jumper that tied the game at 132 at the buzzer to send the game to double-overtime.

Davis fouled out early in the second overtime, which led to Detroit taking a 137-132 lead without Washington's primary big — one they would hold for the remaining of the game.

Young and Davis both finished in double-double territory, but it was not enough to halt Washington's losing streak. Young scored 37 and dished out 14 assists — both season-highs — while Davis scored 30 points and grabbed 14 rebounds. Sarr also tacked on 30 points and seven rebounds, while George scored 14 points and Johnson finished with 13.

Washington is off until Sunday, Nov 15 when it hosts the Houston Rockets at Capital One Arena at 7 p.m. ET on MNMT.

#2706. John Harbaugh expresses confidence in K Dominic Zvada

Giants rookie kicker Dominic Zvada has missed six field goals in nine games. He missed another on Thursday night, a 33-yarder.

While it happened in the first quarter and not on the final play, it stands out in a game that was decided by three points.

After New York’s 24-21 loss to the Commanders, Giants coach John Harbaugh was asked about his level of confidence in Zvada.

“Yeah, we’re confident,” Harbaugh said. “You know, you can’t — as soon as a guy doesn’t make a play, I mean, start firing people left and right. Especially your kicker who’s a rookie. So I’m confident that he’s gonna become a good kicker. I mean, if at some point in time, it doesn’t happen, it doesn’t happen.

“But I’m not gonna panic, you know, halfway through the season when the guy who’s made a bunch of kicks, if that’s what you’re inferring we should be doing.  So, you know, I mean, we’re just not gonna knee-jerk it like that. He’s gonna make kicks. He’s gonna make a lot of kicks, I believe in him.  I think he’s really good, really talented. And we’re gonna give him an opportunity to do it. It’s up to him to do it.”

That’s a fair assessment of a player who’s still new to the NFL. But a kicker has one job. If he can’t do it (especially from distances that should be automatic), at some point tough questions need to be asked.

Basically, how much time will Zvada get before Harbaugh decides it’s not going to happen? That remains to be seen, if Zvada keeps missing kicks he should be making.

#2705. Rangers lose star goaltender Igor Shesterkin for season with lower-body injury; what's next for New York?

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team announced on Saturday.

Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

The 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

Shesterkin was a big reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

Dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

New York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

New York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

The one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a big commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and New York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

However, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether New York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so quickly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of big swings in recent history.
