#2704. Cade Cunningham scores career-high 52 points in Pistons' 144-140 win in 2OT over Wizards

Detroit Pistons guard Cade Cunningham became the first NBA player to record 50 or more points with 10-plus assists and no turnovers in a 144-140 win over the Washington Wizards in double overtime on Thursday.

Turnovers weren't officially recorded by the NBA until 1977, so it isn't certain that Cunningham is the first player to ever post that stat line. However, only three players in the past 49 years — Michael Jordan, Nikola Jokic and Damian Lillard — had scored 50 with 10 assists and 1 turnover. (Hat tip to Yahoo Sports' Dan Devine for that factoid.)

Cunningham finished with a career-high 52 points, shooting 16-of-25 from the floor (including 3-for-5 on 3-pointers) and making 17 of 18 free throws in Detroit's win.

Washington lost — and dropped to 4-9 — despite three players scoring 30 or more points. Trae Young tallied 37 points with 14 assists, while both Anthony Davis and Alex Sarr added 30. Davis also grabbed 15 rebounds and Sarr added 9. The Wizards have lost six consecutive games, including two of their past three to the Pistons.

The Pistons and Wizards played a close game throughout regulation, trading the lead back and forth during the fourth quarter.

With 1.8 seconds left in regulation out of a timeout, Young caught the ball on the right wing and hit a game-tying 3-pointer with two players defending him. It was 121-121.

Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff was not happy about allowing Young's shot, saying "we didn't pay attention to the details."

"We hold ourselves to a higher standard," he added. "In certain moments when we have to be able to generate a stop, we gotta be able to trust each other."

In the first overtime period, the Wizards ran out to a 130-121 lead capped by a Sarr dunk off a lob from Davis. From there, the Pistons went on an 11-2 run — with 7 points from Cunningham — to go back on top. Yet Wizards rookie AJ Dybantsa hit a jumper from the free-throw line to extend the game to another overtime period.

A 3-pointer by Cunningham gave Detroit the advantage in the second overtime, a narrow lead the Pistons would hold until 1:10 remaining when Bilal Coulibaly tied the score at 140-140 on a dunk. Yet Cunningham put the Pistons ahead for good on a midrange jumper with 25 seconds remaining. Two Kevin Huerter free throws gave Detroit its final four-point margin.

"To be able to do what he does in the moment, when it's called on, it's unique and special," Bickerstaff said of Cunningham. "He never ceases to amaze. He just understands what it takes to get it done and has all the abilities to make those things happen."

Daniss Jenkins added 21 points for the Pistons, who improved to 8-3 with the victory. Thompson recorded his first career triple-double with 17 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists, along with 3 steals and 3 blocks.

#2700. Cunningham’s 52 points help the Pistons outlast the Wizards 144-140 in double overtime

Cade Cunningham scored a career-high 52 points and had 11 assists, and the Detroit Pistons outlasted Washington 144-140 in double overtime Thursday night after the Wizards twice extended the game with last-second shots.

Trae Young's 3-pointer at the buzzer forced the first overtime, and then rookie AJ Dybantsa's midrange effort with less than a second left sent the teams to another OT. But Cunningham quickly made a 3-pointer, and then Anthony Davis fouled out to give Detroit the upper hand.

It was still a two-point game in the final minute, but Cunningham scored from the baseline to make it 142-138 with 25.3 seconds left. Washington has lost six straight.

Detroit's Ausar Thompson had 17 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists for his first career triple-double.

Young had 37 points for the Wizards but shot just 8 of 23. Davis and Alex Sarr scored 30 each as the franchise had its first trio of 30-point scorers since Mike Davis, Earl Monroe and Gus Johnson for the Baltimore Bullets on Nov. 18, 1969.

Young had 14 assists, two more than Washington's whole team managed in a loss at Indiana the previous night.

Cunningham's previous career high was 46 points, just over a year ago — and also against Washington. He became the first NBA player with 50 points, 10 assists and no turnovers since the league began tracking turnovers in 1977-78, according to OptaSTATS.

Detroit beat the Wizards for the second time in four games. The Pistons overcame Davis' 44 points to win Monday, and Washington looked ready to end its skid when it scored the first seven points of the first overtime Thursday to lead 128-121. Then Cunningham rallied Detroit.

He finished 16 of 25 from the field and 17 of 18 on free throws. Daniss Jenkins scored 21 points for the Pistons before fouling out. Kyshawn George fouled out for the Wizards after scoring 14.

Sarr was 10 of 10 from the field in regulation and finished 12 of 14.

Pistons: At Miami on Saturday night.Wizards: Host Houston on Sunday night.

#2698. Commanders save season with victory Giants let slip away: TNF winners and losers

EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ — The New York Giants were in the NFC East driver's seat entering their "Thursday Night Football" matchup against the Washington Commanders.

They went on cruise control a little too early in this one.

The Commanders stunned the Giants 24-21 on Nov. 12 to keep their season alive and move within two games of the Giants in the loss column. The game turned from a boring, weather-effected affair into more pleasant conditions with better football. And in the end, it was the Commanders who made more plays.

As always, there were winners and losers within the final result. Let's break it down.

The quarterback made plenty of plays, but the current version of this Commanders team needs him to be Superman to win. He missed Stefon Diggs on a crucial fourth down with nine minutes to play in regulation. He made up for it later.

Daniels wants to win above all. Another loss, effectively ending the Commanders' chances of contention in 2026 – although anything is possible in the NFL – would not sit well with the franchise QB who is eligible for an extension this offseason.

The Washington quarterback did all he could to keep his team competitive despite being the less-talented roster, completing plays like a 30-yard strike to Diggs while rolling to his right and the 1-yard touchdown throw to tight end Ben Sinnott in the second quarter.

Daniels finished 23-of-33 passing for 249 yards and 2 touchdowns. He began running more in the fourth quarter to pick up yardage and rushed 8 times for 30 yards.

For the duration of the game, Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy peppered Likely with targets. But it was the 11th time he sought his tight end's services that the magic happened. On third-and-8 with less than nine minutes left in the fourth quarter, McCarthy fired a bullet over the middle. Likely reached behind himself to catch the ball with both hands but somehow didn't break stride and turned the corner with only the MetLife Stadium turf in front of him.

Likely's 66-yard touchdown gave the Giants a 21-17 lead, and he finished with 9 catches (11 targets) for 127 yards.

Week 3: Indianapolis Colts kicker Spencer Shrader (3) celebrates with long snapper Luke Rhodes (46) after Shrader kicked a 58-yard field goal against the Houston Texans at Lucas Oil Stadium. The Colts debuted their "Anvil Strike" uniform - featuring an unfamiliar gray uniform and glossy, metallic blue helmet with the familiar horseshoe logo in white. The Colts won, 19-17, for their first win of the season.

Week 3: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) hands off to running back James Cook III against the Los Angeles Chargers at New Highmark Stadium. For the game, the Bills debuted their "Nickel City" alternate uniforms - the most striking element being the blue "Charge Helmet," adorned simply with an oversized cutout of the team's familiar logo. The Bills won the game, 24-16.

Week 2: Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford (9) hands the ball to running back Kyren Williams (23) during a 28-6 win on "Monday Night Football" against the New York Giants at SoFi Stadium. The Rams debuted their new "Classic Sol" uniforms, an homage to the team's look during its 1951 championship season.

Week 2: Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett (7) hands off to running back Jeremiyah Love against the Seattle Seahawks at State Farm Stadium. The Cardinals wore their desert-themed "Rivalries" uniforms in the 31-7 loss to the Seahawks. Arizona's "Rivalries" look was one of the best to debut in 2025.

Week 2: The Baltimore Ravens' Trey Hendrickson (91) reacts after a sack against the New Orleans Saints at M&T Bank Stadium. The Ravens wore their "White Noise" uniforms, just one of the team's new uniform combinations that will debut during the 2026 season. The Ravens lost the game, 24-17.

Week 2: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson (5) celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Green Bay Packers at MetLife Stadium. The Jets debuted their "White Out" uniforms for their home opener, which ended in a 20-17 overtime loss.

Week 3: Indianapolis Colts kicker Spencer Shrader (3) celebrates with long snapper Luke Rhodes (46) after Shrader kicked a 58-yard field goal against the Houston Texans at Lucas Oil Stadium. The Colts debuted their "Anvil Strike" uniform - featuring an unfamiliar gray uniform and glossy, metallic blue helmet with the familiar horseshoe logo in white. The Colts won, 19-17, for their first win of the season.

Week 3: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) hands off to running back James Cook III against the Los Angeles Chargers at New Highmark Stadium. For the game, the Bills debuted their "Nickel City" alternate uniforms - the most striking element being the blue "Charge Helmet," adorned simply with an oversized cutout of the team's familiar logo. The Bills won the game, 24-16.

Week 2: Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford (9) hands the ball to running back Kyren Williams (23) during a 28-6 win on "Monday Night Football" against the New York Giants at SoFi Stadium. The Rams debuted their new "Classic Sol" uniforms, an homage to the team's look during its 1951 championship season.

Week 2: Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett (7) hands off to running back Jeremiyah Love against the Seattle Seahawks at State Farm Stadium. The Cardinals wore their desert-themed "Rivalries" uniforms in the 31-7 loss to the Seahawks. Arizona's "Rivalries" look was one of the best to debut in 2025.

Week 2: The Baltimore Ravens' Trey Hendrickson (91) reacts after a sack against the New Orleans Saints at M&T Bank Stadium. The Ravens wore their "White Noise" uniforms, just one of the team's new uniform combinations that will debut during the 2026 season. The Ravens lost the game, 24-17.

Week 2: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson (5) celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Green Bay Packers at MetLife Stadium. The Jets debuted their "White Out" uniforms for their home opener, which ended in a 20-17 overtime loss.

The second-year pro showed up to MetLife wearing an "Iron Man" helmet for no apparent reason. That rules. He then ran like he had a rocket suit on, with 60 yards from scrimmage in the first quarter, his first action back since injuring his hamstring Week 7 against the Houston Texans.

Prime Video reported that he threw up on the bench early in the game and was evaluated by the team's medical staff. He still scored the game's first touchdown with 2:35 to go before halftime on a 1-yard rush that capped a 16-play drive. In typical Skattebo fashion, he absorbed contact at the line of scrimmage before falling forward and extending the ball over the goal line for the score.

Beyond winning a staring contest with the sky camera, Skattebo scored again in the third quarter on a 13-yard pitch play to the right. He was also a factor in the passing game, with three catches for 34 yards. Skattebo averaged 4.3 yards (18 rushes, 78 yards) per carry and was New York's primary back as that role continues to revolve week-to-week.

The Commanders kicker started the season 3-for-5 but is since 13-for-14. He opened the game's scoring with a 46-yard field goal in the second quarter, Stevens' lone attempt of the game.

The hurdle over a defender's outstretched arms is reason enough for the Commanders' third-year tight end to appear in the winners' column. But the career night is the real motivation. Sinnott came into the game with one catch for 6 yards this season but finished with four for 46 yards. He caught Daniels' touchdown pass with five seconds remaining in the first half as the quarterback fell to the ground.

Sinnott had never had more than 3 catches or 36 receiving yards in a game.

Holland, now in his second season with the Giants, hauled in his career-best fourth interception of the season as Daniels attempted to find Chig Okonkwo for the go-ahead touchdown in the fourth.

Washington had a key pass breakup earlier in the game. He finished with six tackles and picked off Daniels with 2:15 remaining and the Giants leading by four.

"Who Let The Dogs Out?" Indeed, Jameis. The backup QB also barked in an effort to get the Commanders to jump offside during a faux fourth-down cadence.

The more severe issue for the Commanders has been the optics. In three games, there have been questionable – at best – game- and clock-management issues. As a head coach that does not call plays on either side of the ball, Quinn has to be more on top of it. He's dealing with a pair of first-time coordinators, to be fair, but he also hired them.

Still, Quinn's team had struggled to execute in late-game scenarios all season but found a way to get it done.

For a brief 15-minute window, fall thunderstorms in northern New Jersey almost threatened to push back the 8:15 p.m. local kickoff time. But the storms passed with enough time to spare and players warmed up amid a light rain before it went away for most of the game.

Thirty-seven of Nabers' 44 yards came on one play. His fumble in the third quarter killed a potential scoring drive and he could not come down with a jump ball in the red zone that would have set up a game-tying field goal that was instead intercepted by Rasul Douglas.

The pair of interceptions at the end of the game nearly doomed his team.

The Giants' rookie kicker may not have his job for long as the team will have a mini-bye to try out potential replacements. The Michigan product started the season 9-for-9 on field goals but has missed six of his last 14 attempts. He was 2-for-5 against Washington during the teams' first meeting.

After Likely's go-ahead touchdown, Zvada booted the kickoff out of bounds – although it was a heads-up play by returner Luke McCaffrey.

His fellow specialist, punter Jordan Stout, shanked a punt that set up the Commanders' game-winning touchdown drive.

#2692. Brewers' Pat Murphy apologized to Yankees' Brian Cashman over viral comment about Jake Bauers free agency

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

In the aftermath of the World Series championship, Brewers manager Pat Murphy was caught on a hot mic talking to first baseman and NLCS MVP Jake Bauers, who heads into free agency this winter off a career year.

Murphy's message? "You're gonna be a rich f---er, but just remember when you were on that horseshit Yankees team and you guys were all playing for yourself, just remember, say, 'this is the way we used to do it.'"

The comment, predictably, drew backlash from those who assumed Murphy was taking a shot at the Yankees. Bauers was on the 2023 Yankees, when they went 82-80 and missed the playoffs.

"I called Brian Cashman right away when I heard it got out," Murphy said on the New York Post's "The Show with Joel Sherman and Jon Heyman released on Tuesday. "I picked up a phone and called Brian right away, and had a good conversation. And the best I could try to explain that I wasn't talking about the 2026 Yankees.

"After every celebration, I'd shake his hand. I'd say, 'You rich so-and-so, you're going to leave us,' " Murphy explained. "We're not going to be able to pay you. You're going to leave us and you're going to forget all about how we did things. … I would just give him this rhetoric every time.

"I was just referring to the teams that have a lot of high-paid, long-contract players," Murphy said. "That sometimes it's harder to get all those guys together to play together. And I used the Yankees because I knew Jake was with them before. … I regret saying it, but that was Jake and I's humor behind the scenes and I got caught."

First off, dudes talking to dudes when they don't realize anyone else is listening lends itself to a lot of comments they don't necessarily mean or, perhaps more importantly, don't include the context of a longstanding relationship between a manager and his player. There isn't anything really out of line here in terms of the Yankees shot. Any Yankees fan would tell you they agree with Murphy's assessment of that team.

Where I do believe there's a problem is the insinuation that a player getting a huge payday means that he'll just start playing only for himself instead of doing things as a team. The Dodgers' high individual salaries certainly didn't stop them from winning two straight World Series titles.

Further, Bauers made $2.7 million last season, double his previous high. MLB players have a finite shelf life and need the money they make to stretch, if they're lucky, for generations. He's set to make exponentially more in free agency in his one big payday to hopefully set up his family for decades. Some might think it insensitive of Murphy to mock that a player might need to look out for himself and his family.

Then again, take note of Murphy's quote when he says that's just their sense of humor. We don't know their personal relationship because it is just that: personal. Unless Bauers signs elsewhere and comes out guns blazing against Murphy, this whole thing is probably just much ado about nothing. It would be pretty shocking if Cashman took particular offense, either.

#2691. OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms

CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State's outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive.

The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU's 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week's matchup with Washington State.

"You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times," Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. "I think it's about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he's at."

The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage.

WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season.

"We don't want to let the verticals up," Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. "We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first."

WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree.

OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays.

"People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage," Dahlen said. "They're going to try and two-hand jam. If they're going to try and two-hand jam, it's like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can't do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can't do it that way.

"That's what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can't just put a safety over the top of him because if he's in the backfield, what are you going to do there?"

Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week.

Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. They're confident they can challenge any defense vertically.

"The underneath throws are going to be there," Hampton said. "We got the best OC in the country; we're going to be able to go deep if we want to."

#2689. Why Packers' Jordan Love is the 2026 midseason MVP: Green Bay QB dominating with no help

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

There is no quarterback in the NFL doing more with less in 2026 than Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love. That's why he is the 2026 midseason NFL MVP through the first nine weeks of the season.

Green Bay has a 6-3 record with wins in five of their last six games, which would have them making the postseason if the season ended today. That is an absolute miracle. The Packers are dead last in the NFL in rushing offense, averaging 68.2 rushing yards per game. That is the fewest rushing yards per game for a team with a winning record through the first nine games of a season in NFL history, and bell cow running back Josh Jacobs is sidelined after undergoing finger surgery.

The Packers have also dropped the most passes, 23, which is seven more than the next closest team. Green Bay's 39 accepted offensive penalties are the third most in the entire league, and the Packers' offensive line is allowing an average time to pressure of 2.48 seconds, the second-fastest in the league, better than only the Carolina Panthers (2.46 seconds). That's because the Packers' best offensive lineman, right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele, went down with a season-ending injury in Week 2, and Green Bay is currently starting their third-string center. Love has also been hit 57 times this season, the fifth most in the league.

All of this is to say Love is doing a lot with not much help around him. He's earned the Packers' winning record.

Despite all those disadvantages and NFL defenses knowing he has to throw it because the Packers can't run it, Love is dominating. On Sunday, he rolled into Gillette Stadium and threw for 372 yards passing and three passing touchdowns while completing 23 of his 29 throws, in addition to adding a 13-yard rushing touchdown. When Packers coach Matt LaFleur subbed in his second-team offense into the game with eight minutes left in the fourth quarter, Green Bay led 45-21. Those 45 points are the most the Patriots have allowed in a home game since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger.

Love is playing quarterback like Ethan Hunt in a "Mission: Impossible" movie. His adversaries know he is coming, and despite the odds stacked against him, Love is still coming out on top. He leads the NFL in passing yards (2,618) and completions of 20-plus yards (40) and is third in the league in passing touchdowns (19). Love is also up to three games with five-plus completions of 30-plus yards this season, which already ranks as the most in any season in the last 35 years.

On Sunday against the Patriots, he also completed six of his eight deep passes, throws of 20-plus air yards, for 235 yards and a touchdown. That was Love's second game with at least six completions of 20-plus air yards in 2026, and no other quarterback in the NFL has done that in any other game this season, per the league's Next Gen Stats.

"I can't say enough about the play of Jordan Love. He makes my job a hell of a lot easier," LaFleur said postgame on Sunday. "He is standing in there, he's taking hits and still dealing the ball. ... Those are low-percentage throws, in theory, but he's making them look high-percentage. They're right on the money."

When you turn on the tape, Love is doing things physically that no other quarterback is doing. In the clip from Sunday below, he is fading off of his back foot with pressure in his face, and he calmly hit wide receiver Christian Watson for a 28-yard gain. This throw isn't an isolated incident for Love either. He makes this pass multiple times a game, week after week.

JORDAN LOVE OFF HIS BACK FOOT FINDS CHRISTIAN WATSONLOVE IS UNSTOPPABLE RIGHT NOW pic.twitter.com/0FNSefZlWc

Buffalo Bills 2024 NFL MVP quarterback Josh Allen, a player some regard as the NFL's best quarterback this season, attempted a similar throw a day later on "Monday Night Football" against the Minnesota Vikings. However, he underthrew the pass for an interception. Even one of the league's most physically gifted passers couldn't execute what Love is doing.

BYRON MURPHY PICKS IT OFF IN THE END ZONEBUFvsMIN on ESPN⁰Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/pJikc7Dtdj

Speaking of the Vikings and their No. 1 defense, no quarterback has thrown for more passing yards (387), yards per pass attempt (9.2), passing touchdowns (2) or a better passer rating (88.1) than Love has against Minnesota's blitzkrieg unit this season.

It's understandable for football fans and media alike to feel fatigued by hearing "the Green Bay Packers have an MVP-caliber quarterback" after Love's predecessors, Brett Favre and Aaron Rodgers, each won at least three league MVP awards. However, Love learned well from Rodgers and Favre. The end result is the Packers quarterback factory cranked out another one. The Packers fans who made the trip out to New England know it. They serenaded him with "MVP" chants as he jogged into the tunnel after Green Bay's 45-27 victory on Sunday.

"It's a really cool feeling, and I really appreciate all the fans," Love said postgame on Sunday.

Making this all the most impressive: The Packers' defense remains without All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons, the unit's best player, who is still rehabbing his knee from a torn ACL and meniscus suffered in December of 2025. Most quarterbacks would crumble into a pile of dust if dropped into these circumstances. Instead, Love has soared and powered the Packers into playoff position. That's why he is the NFL's 2026 midseason MVP.

#2688. The numbers behind Luka Dončić's historic start are entering the realm of ridiculous

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Luka Doncic delivered another casual masterpiece with 53 points in a 124-118 Lakers victory over the Trail Blazers on Friday night. He outscored Portland by himself 20-15 in the third quarter. He dropped a three-quarter-court buzzer-beater to end the first half. He added five rebounds and five assists for fun. And the Lakers are now atop the Western Conference standings at 8-2.

If the season were to end today, Dončić would be the runaway MVP, maybe joining 2015-16 Stephen Curry as the second unanimous winner in NBA history. His box scores will always be somewhat skewed given his usage, but that context notwithstanding, these numbers are downright stupid.

Luka Doncic this season:28 PTS | 8 REB | 7 AST23 PTS | 6 REB | 7 AST52 PTS | 8 REB | 10 AST41 PTS | 5 REB | 9 AST37 PTS | 7 REB | 5 AST45 PTS | 15 REB | 6 AST42 PTS | 7 REB | 13 AST40 PTS | 9 REB | 7 AST53 PTS | 5 REB | 5 ASTMVP? pic.twitter.com/2qjWxSo3E0

Let's dive a little deeper into the numbers behind Dončić's historic start.

Dončić has become the third player in Lakers history to score at least 35 points in seven straight games, joining Kobe Bryant and Elgin Baylor.

Dončić is just the fourth Lakers player to put up four straight 40-point games, joining Bryant, Baylor and George Mikan. You'll notice names like LeBron James, Shaquille O'Neal, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar and Magic Johnson missing from these lists. Some franchise marks are oversold. Not when it comes to the Lakers.

Dončić has made at least five 3-pointers in seven straight games. If he continues that streak for another five games, he will break James Harden's NBA record of 12 straight.

Dončić is currently averaging six made 3-pointers per game. He has played in nine of the Lakers' 10 games. Meaning, if he stays on this pace of six 3s per game while playing in 90% of L.A.'s games, he would end up making 426 3s, which would break Curry's single-season record of 402.

Staying on six, Dončić also owns the non-Wilt Chamberlain NBA record with six 40-point games in his team's first 10 games.

Dončić has now logged seven straight games with at least 35 points, five assists and five rebounds, tying Oscar Robertson for the longest such streak in history.

Dončić is currently attempting 13.7 3-pointers per game. If that volume holds up, it would break Harden's NBA record of 13.2 attempts per game in 2018-19. But Harden only made 36.8% of his 3s that year. Dončić, as you'll see shortly, is blowing that number out of the water.

LUKA DONCIC FROM 3/4 COURT TO END THE HALF. OMG 🤯 pic.twitter.com/6MZGtF5ahY

With two 50-point games so far and just 11% of the schedule completed, Dončić is currently on pace to cook up 16 50-burgers this season, which would shatter Bryant's non-Chamberlain record of 10 in a single season. Chamberlain, for the record, had 45 50-point games in 1961-62, which is just absurd.

After Friday's performance, Dončić is now averaging 40.1 points per game. The only other player in history to average 40 through the first nine games of a season is Chamberlain, who is basically a category unto himself in these statistical side-by-sides. The most Michael Jordan ever averaged through the first nine games of a season was 38.6 in 1986-87.

Dončić is shooting 41.9% from 3 to start the year. That isn't likely to continue. Like Harden, he's been a volume marksman to this point as a career 35% 3-point shooter. But right now he is absolutely dialed, particularly with his step-back, which, according to NBA.com shot tracking, he entered Friday night knocking down at a Curry-like 43% clip.

Luka made 8 of his first 9 three-point attempts last night against the Raptors. Almost all contested step-backs or pull-ups. Crazy level of shot making... pic.twitter.com/K5GWhxXq2x

Dončić is reading the game on autopilot at this point in his career. If you double him, he's zipping the right pass. If you single cover him, he's either powering his way into the paint or, more often, getting right into this step-back as a matter of routine. And when he's making it, there's nothing any defender in the world can do about it.

The Lakers' 110.2 defensive rating with Dončić on the court would register as a top-10 mark. For all the talk about Dončić's poor defense, he hasn't been nearly as bad with the Lakers as he was with the Mavericks (especially in the 2024 Finals, the clips from which are going to haunt him forever), and he's been downright good so far this season.

It's early, yes, and individual defensive stats can be deceiving, but nonetheless Dončić is tied for sixth league-wide with 15 steals (he's been a genuine ball hawk early), and he's tied for the league lead in charges with four.

And get this: Opponents are shooting just 32.3 percent so far with Dončić as their defender, which is the best mark in the league among all players who are defending at least 12 shots per game. Better than Victor Wembanyama!

Again, these can be deceiving markers. Dončić obviously isn't an elite defender, and that opponent shooting percentage is going to vary wildly on Dončić simply being the closest defender on misses rather than the one genuinely forcing someone into a bad shot. Also, he's defending perimeter shots, so on some level, shooters are just missing a lot of shots with him nearby so far.

But the 3-pointers are the ones where he's just the guy closing out a lot (which is still important). Inside the arc, you're much more responsible for effecting misses, and have a look at this entering the Portland game.

SURPRISE LEADER ON DEFENSE: LUKA DONČIĆOpponents have made only 21.9% of their two-point attempts against Luka Dončić this season. No player in the league has allowed a lower mark among those who have defended at least 30 of them.The top 10:Luka Dončić: 21.9%Miles Bridges:… pic.twitter.com/RCnWEqMHg3

Bottom line, a 110.2 defensive rating with Dončić on the floor is what it is. At the very least, he hasn't been a liability, which, given his offensive production, is a major win.

The Lakers' offensive rating with Dončić on the floor this season, which would be an NBA record. When he isn't on the floor, the offense falls to a 99.1 rating, which would rank as the worst in the league by a long shot. As Austin Reaves is finding out in the non-Luka minutes, life is mighty difficult without one of the greatest offensive players in history out there to command all the attention and still break defenses down like a cardboard box.

Including Friday night, the Lakers have won Dončić's on-floor minutes this season by a total of 140 points and lost his bench minutes by 63.

Do the math, and he has single-handedly represented a 203-point swing so far. If you are looking for one MVP number, this might be it.

#2687. Former Yankees, Rangers All-Star Mark Teixeira wins U.S. House seat in Texas

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Former Major League Baseball star Mark Teixeira is headed to Capitol Hill after winning the election for the United States House of Representatives seat in Texas' 21st district on Tuesday. Teixeira, the Republican candidate, beat Democrat Kristin Hook, a former federal scientist.

Teixeira will now take over the seat vacated by Republican Chip Roy, who didn't seek re-election.

"Together, we can build a better future for our families, our neighbors, and every community across Texas 21," Teixeira said in a statement. "I'm excited to get to work. I will be praying for all of you and for the future of this great nation. God bless Texas, and God bless America."

He was a rare win for the GOP in Texas on Tuesday, as Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the gubernatorial race and Democrat James Talarico flipped the Senate seat.

Teixeira, 46, was born and raised in Maryland before attending Georgia Tech as a big-time prospect. He was selected fifth overall in the first round of the 2001 Draft by the Rangers. He then came up through the Rangers' system and spent the first four and a half seasons of his career with the ballclub. He was traded to the Braves in 2007, then to the Angels in 2008 before signing a long-term free agent deal with the Yankees prior to the 2009 season. He finished his career with the Yankees.

In parts of 14 seasons, Teixeira hit .268/.360/.509 (126 OPS+) with 409 home runs, 1,298 RBI, five Gold Gloves, three All-Star Games, three Silver Sluggers and a World Series ring.

Teixeira is one of several familiar sports faces up for election on Tuesday. Former college football coach Tommy Tuberville won the Alabama gubernatorial race and former NFL sideline reporter Michele Tafoya lost the Minnesota Senate race.

This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here.

One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

#2685. Former NFL head coach Rex Ryan arrested by Nashville police for allegedly striking two pedestrians with truck

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Rex Ryan surrendered for booking to Nashville police on Wednesday morning after an incident in which the former NFL head coach allegedly struck two pedestrians with his pickup truck on Thursday, Nov. 5. The two pedestrians suffered minor injuries, according to the police report.

The incident occurred before midnight that Thursday as the pedestrians were crossing Broadway and 4th Avenue with a walk sign on. Ryan, 63, allegedly turned right from 4th Avenue and ran over both victims' feet. Ryan's truck also made contact with one of the individuals' legs.

According to the pedestrians, the vehicle kept driving after striking them, but stopped at a red light at Broadway and Representative John Lewis Way.  That's when they waved Ryan down, and the former coach is said to have stepped out of his truck to argue with them before getting back in and driving away. They took pictures of the drive and the truck's license plate, which was registered to Ryan.

After surrendering for booking on Wednesday morning, Ryan was charged with two counts of leaving the scene of an accident, two counts of failure to give information/render aid, and two counts of failure to obey a traffic control device. Ryan's bond was set by a judicial commissioner at $6,000.

Ryan last coached in the NFL back in 2016 when he was head coach of the Buffalo Bills. Before that, he broke into the league as a defensive line and linebackers coach for the Arizona Cardinals back in 1994. From there, he went on to become a decorated defensive-minded coach. He spent the bulk of his career in Baltimore, beginning as a defensive line coach in 1999 before ascending to defensive coordinator in 2005 and holding that position until 2008, before being hired as the head coach of the New York Jets.

Ryan was on staff during Baltimore's Super Bowl XXXV championship and is 65-68 in his head coaching career (4-2 in the playoffs).

#2683. MLB rumors: The only Oriole not on the trading block, Rays' Drew Rasmussen plan and Astros add to manager hunt

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The Brewers have now been World Series champions for just one week (minus a few hours) and they should still be basking in the glory for quite a while. As the offseason marches on, the next big date will be Nov. 17, when decisions on qualifying offers are due from the eight players who received one.

In the meantime, the rumor mill should be ever-so-slowly churning. We'll round it up here.

The Houston Astros moved on from general manager Dana Brown in August and fired manager Joe Espada after the 2026 season. Newly hired general manager Randy Flores is now tasked with landing a new dugout boss, and a three-time MVP and future Hall of Famer is in the mix. The Astros will interview Albert Pujols for the manager job this week, per The Athletic.

Pujols has long made it known that he desires to be an MLB manager. He recently interviewed for vacancies with the Padres and Angels (both last offseason) and he also managed the Dominican Republic in the World Baseball Classic this past spring. It should be further noted that Pujols is in the fourth year of a 10-year, $100 personal services contract with the Angels that was part of the mega-deal he signed with them as a player prior to the 2012 season as a player.

Other known candidates for the Astros manager job are Rangers bench coach Luis Urueta and Yankees bench coach (not to mention former Tigers and Angels manager) Brad Ausmus. Former Astros third baseman Morgan Ensberg, the manager of the Triple-A Rays affiliate Durham Bulls, will also interview this week, according to MLB.com.

The Orioles are willing to listen to trade offers on any player other than Pete Alonso as they seek both rotation and outfield help, according to The Baltimore Banner. The  Orioles reportedly aren't "actively shopping" any players, but they are looking for upgrades at starting pitcher and outfielder and realize one of the ways that could happen is via a trade.

Surely they wouldn't sell low on Gunnar Henderson, given his immense upside, so we can probably take him off the table unless some team makes it worth their while. There is a glut of infielders, though. With Alonso at first base and Henderson at short, they have Jackson Holliday, Christian Encarnacion-Strand, Jordan Westburg and Coby Mayo for two spots. Even using one of the four at designated hitter, it's easy to see where a deal could happen.

Westburg and Encarnacion-Strand are under team control through 2029 while Holliday is controlled through 2030 and Mayo through 2031.

The American League champion Rays recently picked up the $20 million club option on All-Star starting pitcher Drew Rasmussen. That would be a franchise-record salary for one player in a single season. It might seem odd to exercise an option and then deal a player to an outsider, but locking Rasmussen in for a one-year deal makes him an attractive trade candidate instead of just letting him walk in free agency, and this is how the Rays generally operate. We've seen it so many times: they get ahead of losing guys to free agency, sometimes even dealing them a year or two earlier. They've done it with Randy Arozarena, Isaac Paredes, Tyler Glasnow and even going back to franchise legends like David Price, Evan Longoria and Ben Zobrist.

The Rays right now are saying they intend to keep Rasmussen for 2027.

"Not a declarative this, that, whatever, but I can sit here very confidently and say that every intention right now is thinking about Ras anchoring our rotation and how to make this team better going into next year," club president Erik Neander said on Tuesday, via the Tampa Bay Times.

If they want to contend again next year, it sure seems like they need Rasmussen, with Nick Martinez and Freddy Peralta off to free agency. That leaves Rasmussen atop the rotation, followed by Shane McClanahan, Griffin Jax, Ryan Pepiot and a bunch of question marks. There are questions attached to McClanahan, Jax and Pepiot too.

#2682. Dame Time is back in Portland — and the Blazers look dangerous

A new head coach will roam the sidelines. A franchise icon will make his long-awaited return. An All-Star will begin his redemption tour.

And a new ownership group will watch its first season opener from Paul Allen's former seats along the Moda Center baseline.

The Blazers open the 2026-27 NBA season Wednesday night against the Phoenix Suns — a team they upset in April in the play-in tournament — and if you're just now tuning in for the start of the regular season, well, there's a lot you missed.

RELATED: Suns vs. Blazers predictions, odds and best bets: Dame is home, and the model likes Portland on opening night

The Blazers are expected to unveil a new starting lineup that features a pair of notable All-Star additions: Damian Lillard and Ja Morant. The backcourt duo is joining a fivesome that includes returning starters Deni Avdija, Toumani Camara and Donovan Clingan. It's a versatile, star-studded lineup that features three All-Stars, a former All-Defensive Second Team selection, one of the best young centers in the NBA and loads of scoring potential.

Micah Nori, the Blazers' first-year head coach, said he plans on using a 10-man rotation to start the season, which will allow the Blazers to capitalize on their depth and versatility. In addition to the starters, Jrue Holiday, Scoot Henderson, Sidy Cissoko, Robert Williams III and Vit Krejci are expected to open the season in the rotation. The group could change depending on matchups and Williams' availability — he did not play in back-to-backs last season — and it's likely that Micah Potter, Branden Carlson and Yang Hansen will occasionally see spot duty, as well.

The Blazers stabilized their turbulent coaching situation in June, hiring longtime NBA assistant Nori to replace interim coach Tiago Splitter. Nori, who interviewed for head coaching jobs seven times before finally landing his first chance, is entering his 29th season in the league and is universally revered in NBA circles for his positive approach, ability to connect with players and sharp basketball mind. Early indications have been encouraging, as the Blazers players seem to love him and the front office works well with him. The Blazers' coaching position had been embroiled in controversy, of course, as former coach Chauncey Billups — who was placed on indefinite leave by the NBA — is facing federal felony charges related to money laundering and wire fraud conspiracy for his alleged involvement in a rigged underground poker game.

In a stark contrast to recent seasons, the Blazers are constructed around their offense rather than their defense. The roster is unbalanced, featuring five dynamic ball-handlers and playmakers (Lillard, Morant, Avdija, Holiday and Henderson), a solid center combination (Clingan and Williams) and little wing depth. As a result, the team is expected to play fast and free under Nori, bringing lots of speed, passing, cutting and flow. Nori said he hopes to rotate his players liberally in shorter shifts during games — perhaps as short as three minutes — which will enable them to play with maximum effort before giving way to teammates. The interior defense is strong with Clingan and Williams patrolling the middle, Camara remains one of the NBA's best and most versatile defenders and Cissoko will be asked to guard one-through-five. Holiday is still capable of locking down opposing guards and Avdija has pledged to be more of a two-way threat now that he doesn't have to serve as the team's primary ball-handler. But the backcourt combination of Morant and Lillard, while lethal on offense, is not imposing on defense and relatively small (both stand 6-foot-2).

Portland defied pundits last season, winning 10 of its last 14 regular season games to secure a spot in the play-in tournament, where it beat the Suns in Phoenix to earn the seventh seed in the Western Conference. The San Antonio Spurs dismissed the Blazers with a gentleman's sweep in the playoffs, but the strong run — combined with the additions of Lillard and Morant — has raised expectations in Portland. How much? Camara said in training camp that the Blazers' goal is to win 50 or more games and secure home-court advantage in the postseason. It won't be easy. The league is as deep and talented as ever, and new rules surrounding the lottery should discourage teams from tanking, meaning most of the league will be chasing wins instead of lottery ping-pong balls late into the season. It seemed like a third of the league had given up last year by the All-Star break.

Joe Freeman's 3 takeaways from the Trail Blazers' back-to-back sweep vs. Thunder

Trail Blazers lose rotation player for 2 months

Joe Freeman's 3 takeaways from Trail Blazers' rout over the Thunder

Thunder vs. Blazers predictions: Portland looks to snap two-game skid in the first of back-to-back meetings

Joe Freeman's 3 takeaways from Trail Blazers' lopsided loss to Spurs

As the Blazers' new-look lineup works to build chemistry and a first-year coach settles into a new role, the schedule will be challenging. Six of the first eight games — and 12 of the first 17 — will come on the road and include a slew of playoff contenders, including the Spurs, Oklahoma City Thunder (twice), Minnesota Timberwolves (twice), New York Knicks, Philadelphia 76ers, Denver Nuggets and Los Angeles Lakers (twice).

The most uplifting part of opening night figures to be the return of Lillard, the franchise icon who is back after spending two seasons in Milwaukee and one season on the injured list. The nine-time All-Star and franchise leader has not played in an NBA regular-season or playoff game since April 27, 2025, when he suffered a torn left Achilles tendon. And he has not played with Portland since March 22, 2023, six months before it traded him to the Bucks. Lillard showed no ill effects from his injury during the exhibition season, when he played in three of the Blazers' four games and averaged 17.3 points, 2.7 assists and 22.7 minutes. If anything, he looked like the same old Dame, swishing three-pointers, creating off the dribble, initiating offense and drawing defensive attention. Lillard joked earlier this week that he's "not an old man," but also acknowledged that he isn't likely to play upward of 38 minutes a game like he used to and may even take a night off here and there for rest, most likely on a random back-to-back. His addition not only should help cover up two of the Blazers' biggest weaknesses last season — three-point shooting and shooting in the clutch — but also inspire a thirsty fan base, which has rarely loved a player more. All the while, Lillard says he intends to play with more "joy" than ever.

#2681. Cavaliers coach Kenny Atkinson explains infamous 'analytically' quote during playoffs loss to Knicks

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

NBA players regularly draw scrutiny for things they say to the press, but coaches tend to be reserved enough to avoid getting too much egg on their faces. Kenny Atkinson is a recent exception; the Cleveland Cavaliers coach has been mocked for the past six months or so for his now-infamous comments after Game 3 of the Eastern Conference Finals.

With the Cavaliers down 3-0 to the New York Knicks, Atkinson was asked how he could give hope to his players, as no team in NBA history has ever overcome a 3-0 series deficit. "Analytically … we've won 2 out of 3," Atkinson said at the time. "We're two out of the three in the expected score. If you believe in process and all that, like, man, take that later. I don't throw that on them. I see it for myself, and if I have this feeling, I can go to our analytical table and be like, man, the expected score was like one point or two — us shooting way below expected, them shooting way over."

As Atkinson explained, analytics can estimate what a game's score should have been based on the shots both teams managed to produce and the expected field goal percentage of those shots. Essentially, if both teams shot exactly as the numbers suggest they would over a long sample, this is what the score would be. Atkinson did not specify which games he meant out of the three, but it was likely Game 1, which Cleveland lost in overtime, and Game 3, which New York won, 121-113. Prime Stats has an expected score metric that had Game 3 at a 113-113 tie, and while New York had an expected 10-point win in Game 1, that accounts for overtime. If the actual score had matched what Cleveland's analytics department projected in regulation, the game never would have gotten an extra period and the Cavaliers would have gone up 1-0.

Obviously, despite the expected scores, the Knicks led the series 3-0 at that point and had won those games by 40 total points. They went on to win Game 4 by 37 points, 130-93, though if it's any consolation, the Prime Stats expected score was a slightly less embarrassing 125-100. Both before the Game 4 sweep and afterward, Atkinson's quote was widely mocked. That includes jabs by multiple Knicks, as Josh Hart joked that "I guess we lost analytically" on his podcast with Jalen Brunson, and Karl-Anthony Towns, who said before the ESPYs that "analytically, we should win" the Best Team award. The word "analytically" has become shorthand for anyone attempting to justify an ugly defeat using numbers.

On Saturday, the Cavaliers faced the Knicks for the first time since that series. New York won again, 109-97, and yet again, the expected score was slightly more favorable to Cleveland, with Prime Stats posting an expected score of 112-103. Atkinson did not point to those numbers after Saturday's defeat. Instead, he attempted to explain the widely derided quote, arguing that the quote was taken out of context, which made the soundbite sound less flattering than his actual answer was.

"I would just say there was no coach more complimentary of the Knicks and honest about our performance and how they dominated us," Atkinson told reporters. "So you live and learn a little bit with those things. But like I said, 99% of my comments were how they dominated us. They were by far the better team. I answered the question, as it was taken, [which was] 'And you're down 3-0, what hope do you have of even giving to your guys?'

"We get a lot of information … and I wasn't lying in that sense, but in no sense was it like, 'Oh, man, we deserve to be winning.' Like zero — zero — thought of that."

Atkinson acknowledged that "no one wants to hear" about process when the outcome is a blown 22-point fourth-quarter lead and a 3-0 deficit, but he was trying to figure out how to rally his troops in an impossible situation. His phrasing has become a meme, but when you're down 3-0 in the playoffs, you'll grasp at any signs of positivity you can find. Atkinson had numbers suggesting the two teams were closer than the scoreboard suggested. Using those numbers to try to inspire his team made sense. Putting them out there in public risked exactly the sort of ridicule he ultimately got. The soundbite eclipsed the quote and the context, and the rest is history.

#2678. Biggest MLB offseason questions: How long will lockout last? Will we see a free agency frenzy?

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Not so long ago, the Milwaukee Brewers were crowned World Series champions, and at the moment of the last out, the 2026-27 Major League offseason began. So let's talk about that.

The winter ahead is one shot through with uncertainty, as labor strife figures to roil the sport and perhaps even compromise the 2027 season. Those matters, vital as they are, won't be the only story, and we'll still have the familiar presences of free agency and trade talk to sustain us.

To set the scene for all that's ahead in advance of the 2027 campaign – good, ill, or somewhere in the middle – we're here to take a look at the five questions that will inform an offseason that's going to be quite unusual and – for good, ill, or somewhere in the middle – probably unforgettable. Let's explore those five queries right now …

The current collective bargaining agreement – or CBA, the accord that governs the working relationship between clubs/owners and players – is set to expire at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1 of this year. At that time, MLB owners are all but certain to lock out the players. That's a labor stoppage, and that means the offseason will be brought to a sudden halt. The lockout, the purpose of which is to preempt a players' strike, will last until a new CBA is agreed to. Agreeing to a new CBA will be no simple matter, and owners and their hireling, commissioner Rob Manfred, are pushing for a cap on team payrolls. The players, as represented by their union, the MLBPA, have never shown any willingness to agree to a cap-and-floor system. There are a lot of other issues to iron out, as the CBA is an all-encompassing document, but the fight over a cap will be what drags out the lockout.

The heart of the matter is whether the lockout will last long enough to push back, abbreviate, or – perish the thought – cancel entirely the 2027 season. The latter is the worst-case scenario and is highly unlikely, but it's a possibility, however remote. More of a threat is a 2027 season that doesn't span the usual 162 games.

We have a recent precedent to guide us. The last time the CBA was up for negotiation during the offseason of 2021-22, owners locked out the players for 99 days. That meant a shortened spring training by about two and a half weeks and forced the regular season calendar to be compressed, albeit while still preserving the 162-game docket. As such, we can say that if the lockout lasts beyond the middle of March 2027, then we'll likely lose regular-season games.

For further context, here's a brief history of modern labor stoppages in the sport:

Just two, the 1981 and 1994-95 player strikes, significantly compromised seasons. The 1994-95 stoppage cost us the 1994 World Series, and it took years for the sport to recover from the resulting fan disaffection.

As for the 2027 season, the worst-case scenario may not be the loss of the entire season but rather the loss of 60 games off the regular-season slate. Here's the explanation from our recent Lockout 101 piece:

"… [I]f the lockout extends into late May or so and costs at least 60 games, then most of the league's national broadcast and streaming contracts would be extended for another year, through 2029. That matters because Manfred and the league hope to bundle and centralize team streaming rights and share those revenues equally, and the current timeline would theoretically allow that to happen at the same time the national contracts are up for renegotiation in 2028. Tacking on another year to those national contracts would push back the significant windfall that owners and the league are expecting from that new media rights structure. This amounts to a major incentive, at least on the league side, to agree to a new CBA before June arrives."

Obviously, the hope is that the lockout doesn't even affect the spring training calendar, let alone cost us a major chunk of the regular season.

As noted, the big fight is over whether or not MLB will have a cap-and-floor structure moving forward, as is the case in the NFL, NBA, and NHL. Owners have tied every single proposal wrinkle to date to the players' acceptance of a cap. However, it remains highly unlikely, at least until further notice, that the union would ever agree to such a thing.

The other major issue is a likely restructuring of the revenue-sharing system. Specifically, the next CBA is highly likely to revise the system so that local broadcast revenues are shared much more evenly. Fortunately, there's already some common ground on this issue, and a reordering of that system would directly address the revenue disparities within MLB that are such a reliable source of consternation – and misinformation – without the grievous labor war that a continued cap push would force upon us.

Otherwise, some other key wrinkles and changes may come out of the wash. That list potentially includes:

This doesn't get into evergreen matters like an increase in the minimum salary, draft bonus pools, the qualifying offer system, active roster sizes, and so forth. There's a lot to sort out, to say the least. The expectation is that the next CBA is going to lead to sweeping changes to the sport starting in 2027 and, perhaps by design, growing over time. Even if there's no cap and floor, the economic structure of MLB is almost certain to look very different after this winter.

Overall, this is one of the weakest free agent classes in living memory, but there is elite superstar value to be found at the tip-top with back-to-back (for the moment) American League Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal.

Skubal, who turns 30 on Nov. 20, remains foremost in the discussion for best pitcher in baseball, and he's going to be paid like it. The expectation is that he'll wind up signing the largest pitcher contract in MLB history and perhaps also fetch the highest-ever annual salary for a pitcher. It's not out of the question that Skubal's next contract could approach or even surpass $400 million in total value. At those rates, the incumbent Los Angeles Dodgers and the free-spending New York Mets are the consensus favorites. The Chicago Cubs are also reportedly heavily interested in Skubal, and surprise bidders are always possible. Other notable free agent names include Freddy Peralta, Michael King, Jazz Chisholm Jr., Trevor Rogers, Adrian Morejon, and Teruaki Sato. Our ranking of the top 50 2026-27 free agents has you covered.

The "when" of all this is more complicated thanks to the upcoming lockout detailed above. Will premium free agents and their representatives rush to find some stability in advance of the stoppage, during which no major-league transactions will be permitted, or will they decide that the long game will be better for their markets? It's possible that the biggest spenders on the team side will look to make moves early, as the barrel of the next CBA figures to be leveled directly at them and their abundant revenues. Or maybe the unknown will have a chilling effect on spending before we arrive at the lockout.

The past is not always prelude, but let's note that we saw a flurry of spending leading up to the lockout of 2021-22. Indeed, in November 2021, MLB teams committed more than $1.7 billion to free agents prior to the lockout. The Texas Rangers alone guaranteed $500 million to a new middle infield – Corey Seager and Marcus Semien – before the lockout put an end to such things. In all, teams put ink to paper on five nine-figure contracts prior to the 2021-22 lockout.

The comparisons may not entirely hold since this upcoming CBA should bring about a much more drastic re-ordering of the sport than the current expiring CBA did. As such, teams may proceed cautiously given all the uncertainties. Or, as just mentioned, they may seek to get business done before the ways of doing business change entirely. We'll see soon enough. If we do see the dollars start flying before the lockout, then the upcoming Nov. 10-12 general managers meetings in Las Vegas may occasion the groundwork for all those deals.

Will a lackluster free agent class mean more headline-grabbing trades? That may indeed be answered in the affirmative this winter. Yes, the CBA uncertainty will have a bearing on trades, especially those that involve the assumption of major salary obligations, but big trades still figure to be a prominent part of this offseason.

It's of course impossible to know who's going to be dealt ahead of time, but some big names perhaps on the move this winter include Francisco Lindor, Mason Miller, Spencer Strider, Hunter Greene, Otto Lopez, Jeremy Peña, Ketel Marte, Jacob deGrom, and of course others. Paul Skenes? Almost certainly not, but you'll just as certainly hear his name bandied about.

Turning back to last lockout, it was mostly minor trades before the sport shut down. Yes, we'll see big ones this time around, but they may not happen until we have a new CBA in place and the lockout is over.

Let's make time for the losers, shall we? The teams that didn't make the postseason in 2026 and otherwise qualify will take part in the draft lottery, which is presently scheduled for Dec. 8. That lottery will determine which teams get the top six picks in the 2027 MLB Draft.

This year, 16 of the 18 non-playoff teams will be in the lottery. Non-playoff teams can be barred from the lottery if they've had lottery picks in two consecutive seasons. If a team is a revenue-sharing payor, then it can't be in the lottery in consecutive years. Those wrinkles this year mean that the San Francisco Giants and Pittsburgh Pirates will not be in the lottery and can't pick higher than 10th in the 2027 Draft.

Here's how the preliminary lottery odds look for those 16 teams in the mix, based on how they finished the 2026 season:

It's too soon to know which players will be in the mix for that top pick since the amateur seasons haven't begun yet. However, two early favorites to go No. 1 are University of Florida shortstop Brendan Lawson and Mississippi State left-hander Tomas Valinicius.

Injuries haven't helped, with the likes of Kevin Fiala, Alex Turcotte and Mats Zuccarello all on injured reserve. #2675. NFL trade deadline: Jonathan Taylor leads candidates for offseason moves after staying put

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The deals that got across the finish line at the 2026 NFL trade deadline included a couple of blockbusters that shook up the balance of power at the front of the Super Bowl race. But just as meaningful were the moves that never materialized. For instance, the Cincinnati Bengals and Philadelphia Eagles called off an agreed-upon transaction that would have bolstered the former's defense. Even more significant than the nixed Arnold Ebiketie deal were the offers for Jonathan Taylor and other stars that never resulted in trades, either.

Taylor was supposed to be the belle of the ball at the deadline, but the Indianapolis Colts turned down interest from other teams when they did not receive the first-round pick they sought in a return package. Stars like George Pickens and other players like Will McDonald IV who would have been plug-and-play starters on other teams remained in place on their present rosters.

The players teams made and entertained calls on but did not switch at the deadline immediately became names to monitor ahead of the next trade window, which opens in the spring at the start of the 2027 league year.

Here are the 10 biggest names that did not change teams at the trade deadline but who could be on the move in the offseason.

The Indianapolis Colts were the most aggressive sellers at the trade deadline, but Jonathan Taylor was not among the four players they shipped out of town. The three-time Pro Bowler is a gargantuan asset because he is an elite-tier running back with no guaranteed money on his contract in 2027 or 2028, so he can remain an affordable and prolific foundational piece of the Colts' rebuild. Those same factors make him tremendously valuable on the trade market, though, and for a team that is going nowhere fast, it would behoove the Colts to take the right deal if it came to them in the offseason. They reportedly turned down offers that included second-round picks and more, so it will probably take at least a first-rounder to pry him away next spring or summer.

Unless the Dallas Cowboys re-sign George Pickens, they may regret not trading him. They likely could have garnered a sizable return package for their No. 2 wide receiver -- who would be a No. 1 on most teams -- and that would have arguably been the more prudent move than keeping him on a squad that is on the outside looking in on the playoff picture. Jerry Jones declined to sign Pickens to a long-term extension last offseason and could again use the franchise tag on the standout pass-catcher, but Pickens is worthy of a lucrative multi-year deal and may seek one elsewhere if Jones is hesitant again.

Will McDonald IV requested a trade from the New York Jets on the eve of the trade deadline, citing frustration with his playing time. He played 50% or more of the team's defensive snaps just three times over the first nine weeks and most recently saw only 24 snaps of work in Week 9. Darren Mougey did not heed his request, though, and retained him despite reported interest from other teams, including the Jacksonville Jaguars. New York has myriad options at edge rusher and will feature David Bailey most prominently in the years to come, so a clear path to a larger role may not manifest for McDonald. In that case, he could amplify his search for a trade in the offseason.

A reunion between Khalil Mack and the Chicago Bears would have made all the sense in the world, but the Los Angeles Chargers showed no interest in moving him, and the Bears used their draft capital on Jeffery Simmons instead. That the Chargers held onto all but one player despite their putrid 0-8 record was a major surprise. There were draft picks to be had for Mack, Ladd McConkey and even Justin Herbert, but the Chargers elected to keep their core intact even as it looks unsalvageable in a miserable campaign. Mack is a prime candidate to walk in free agency since he is in the latter stages of his career and would thus be more likely to seek a home on a contending squad rather than a bottom-dweller like Los Angeles.

Teams inquired about Tony Pollard, but none constructed a trade package strong enough for the Tennessee Titans to move on from him. The 29-year-old's value has never been higher on the heels of back-to-back 100-yard performances in which he totaled five touchdowns, and that could have played a role in the Titans driving a hard bargain. Retaining him is a short-term play that will allow Tennessee to continue to evaluate second-year quarterback Cam Ward but may not be much more than that since Pollard can leave in free agency if he pleases. At 29, he is not on the same career timeline as the rest of the team's offensive building blocks, anyway.

It makes ample sense for the Jacksonville Jaguars to hold onto anyone and everyone as they prepare for a potential Super Bowl run. If it ain't broke, don't fix it. But Brian Thomas Jr. is only a marginal part of their stellar passing attack and lost ground to Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers in the pecking order for targets. His Pro Bowl-caliber rookie season looks more and more like a flash in the pan. Unless the Jaguars truly believe they can maximize the former first-round pick's talent in the final year of his contract, his situation will be one to revisit in the next trade window that opens in March. This is not dissimilar to the situation that led to Marvin Harrison Jr. being traded to the Houston Texans for a second-round pick and sixth-rounder, but the Jaguars are a contender and would reasonably prefer not to toy with their lineup until after the season.

Budda Baker is an Arizona Cardinals legend. If the 2026 trade deadline—when the Cardinals are projected as potential sellers amid on-field struggles —was not the time to move him, they may just let him play out his career in the desert. As the Cardinals' roster continues to shift in a younger direction, though, a split could make sense. Baker will be 31 when the 2027 league year begins, and the Cardinals are poised to take a quarterback in the first round of the draft, restarting the clock on their contention timeline. As an eight-time Pro Bowler still in his prime, Baker would garner the kind of return that would help Arizona load up on draft picks and build around that incoming quarterback.

As with the other trade candidates on expiring deals, Riq Woolen's potential exit in free agency could net the Philadelphia Eagles a valuable compensatory draft pick. That is probably the justification for keeping him, because Howie Roseman was willing to move on from some foundational pieces in the weeks leading up to the deadline, and Woolen seemed as tradeable as any of them. Woolen has been solid for the Eagles in pass defense but regressed from the standout level he performed at with the Seattle Seahawks -- his 103.3 passer rating allowed is by far a career-worst -- so Philadelphia may not aim to retain him on a multi-year deal regardless.

There have been rumblings of a possible Josh Sweat trade since the spring. Nothing came to fruition in the offseason, and the Arizona Cardinals stood pat at the trade deadline, too. But as the team remains mired in the early stages of a deep rebuild, any tensions between Sweat and the front office may grow louder in advance of his next opportunity to seek a way out. Sweat reportedly requested a trade last spring amid frustration with his contract, but both he and the team worked to quell that narrative over the last handful of months. It is clear that moving him is not a top priority for the Cardinals, but the standout pass rusher will be one to keep monitoring at the start of the new league year in 2027 in case that changes.

The Tennessee Titans have phased Calvin Ridley out of their receiving corps, with Carnell Tate, Wan'Dale Robinson, Elic Ayomanor, and Chimere Dike outproducing him in catches. Two tight ends and two running backs also have more targets than him this season. If he is no longer part of their plans, it makes little sense to retain him for the final year of his $92 million contract. His dead cap hit shrinks from $22.5 million to $7.5 million this spring, so if the idea behind keeping him on the roster is to maximize future financial flexibility, that decrease in liability should free things up on the books enough to move on from him at the start of the next league year.

#2674. Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind

EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks. One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished.

Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season.

"One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity," sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said.

After his team's 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward.

On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability.

"I've been proud of the way that they've worked," Lanning said. "I don't see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that's challenging, too, especially when you're young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief."

Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian

The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26.

That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings.

Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year's semifinal squad.

RELATED: Can the Ducks bounce back from UCLA loss? Experts release new Oregon vs. Nebraska predictions

It's not uncommon for teams with grand expectations to unravel in tough times. So far, that hasn't happened.

"The team is very connected and maintains its composure whether we're winning or losing," punter Bailey Ettridge said. "We haven't let the losses last week and against Oklahoma State bring us down. I think we've handled them well."

Wide receiver Dakorien Moore said the team is filled with players who came to Oregon to win and be great. He added that the team's goals remain attainable, and team leaders have worked to encourage togetherness and mutual trust.

"If you can't trust your teammate, then everything ain't going to form in the way that it's supposed to," he said.

This also means trusting the process, the plan and the team's goal to get better instead of blaming one another.

Oregon head coach Dan Lanning talks to the defense during a timeout as the No. 13 Oregon Ducks face the No. 21 UCLA Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian

"Everybody knows what we want to attack this next week, being that Nebraska is a good team," he said.

The outside noise has been deafening. To say that many Oregon fans have melted down on social media would be an understatement.

Virtually all of the players have social media accounts. Moore said he is active on social media but ignores negativity.

Finney said he isn't very active on social media and doesn't care what people say outside the program.

"Why would I let your opinion inflict me or my thoughts on my performance or my thoughts on our performance," he said. "Because people are going to be there when you're doing good, when you're bad; when you're doing bad, they're going to leave you."

For that reason, the team lives by the motto F.E.B.U., which stands for "Forget Everyone But Us".

"F.E.B.U. is a true statement that we all follow," Finney said. "… Just back to work. We got to figure out what we did wrong, go to the doctor, and just get back to work."

Fifth-year linebacker Devon Jackson said before the season that his main goal was team-driven — winning the national title.

"At the end of the year, what happens, happens, but I promise if we focus on the day and focus on one game at a time, we will be okay," Jackson said.

On Saturday, the Ducks' defense played one of its best games of the season, while the offense played its worst without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who remains in concussion protocol.

On teams that lack closeness, such a contrast can cause issues. But that is not the case with Oregon.

"I mean, we're all in this together," Jackson said. "It's not like, the defense won the game and offense lost, or special teams won or lost. We all lost together and we all win together. So, we got each other's back no matter what."

Oregon offensive players celebrate a touchdown run by running back Jordon Davison (#0) as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 UCLA Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The OregonianSean Meagher/The Oregonian

Jackson said that after Saturday's loss, he and senior center Iapani Laloulu talked for 20 minutes about the team. He told Laloulu that he didn't care what was going on with the offense; the defense had its back.

"I wouldn't trade that group with anybody else in the country despite what other people may think," Jackson said. "And we're going to continue to lean on each other because it's we all we got and we all we need."

Realistically, Oregon can't expect much sympathy from outsiders. The Ducks have top-notch facilities, infinite uniform options, a roster with an estimated payroll of $50 million, and a coach who isn't afraid to speak his mind, as Lanning did after beating the Trojans.

Many in the football world certainly wouldn't mind seeing Oregon fall.

"Ain't nobody going to feel sorry for us," linebacker Matayo Uiagalelei said. "So just came back in the next day with the mindset ready to work."
