#2639. Buyer Beware: 5 NFL deadline trades that could become the next Sauce Gardner bust

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

As in-season trades become all the more prevalent in the NFL, the risk of overspending also rises. That was most clear in 2025 when the Indianapolis Colts made perhaps the most regrettable trade in league history by sending two first-round picks to the New York Jets in exchange for cornerback Sauce Gardner. Those draft picks are golden with the Colts entering a deep rebuild, while Gardner has played the worst football of his career since landing in Indianapolis.

When teams pulled off 18 deals ahead of the 2026 trade deadline, they did so hoping to avoid the disaster that was the Colts' acquisition of Gardner. Chances are high that none of this year's trades will be as lopsided as that one, but it is far too soon to rule it out.

Only one transaction this year included two first-round picks, and it is already paying dividends for the purchasing side. And only one other included a single first-rounder. That does not mean that all of the teams involved are out of the woods just yet, though.

Here are the 2026 in-season trades with the greatest potential to go down as busts.

The trade that most resembles the infamous Sauce Gardner deal is the one that moved Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears. The Tennessee Titans secured two first-round picks in the swap. There will always be long-term risks (most notably regarding injury), but Simmons has already delivered, in a small sample size, everything the Bears could have asked of him. The superstar defensive tackle notched a sack and pass breakup in both of his first two games and logged an additional tackle for loss in his debut and elevated the entire unit around him in the process. It is far too soon to close the book on this trade, but all indications suggest it is a slam dunk for the Super Bowl-contending Bears.

Many elements of the Jordan Davis trade make sense for the Jacksonville Jaguars as they pursue the first Super Bowl in franchise history. The most obvious of them is that Davis fills an immediate need that arose when DaVon Hamilton went down with a season-ending torn quad muscle. But there is a great deal of inherent risk that comes with moving a 2027 first-round pick and 2029 second-rounder to land him. It is an all-in move that will either pay tremendous dividends or go down as an overpay. There is very little middle ground when it comes to these kinds of blockbuster trades.

Davis has to be a difference-maker from the jump. The Jaguars are in play for the AFC's No. 1 seed and will battle until season's end to secure it. More importantly, this trade will be judged in the context of what Davis delivers in the postseason. Anything short of a Super Bowl run is suddenly a disappointment, and Davis needs to play a major role in their championship pursuit.

From a run-stopping standpoint, Davis should give the Jaguars everything they lost from Hamilton and more. For the price they paid, it would be preferable if Davis were more of a threat as a pass rusher, however. He has never logged more than 4.5 sacks in a season. If offenses have to take blockers away from other players to account for him, then perhaps the added pocket disruption from the edges will make up for his lack of havoc creation.

The 2023 Biletnikoff Award winner is already a bust of a No. 4 overall draft pick. Will his trade from the Arizona Cardinals to the Houston Texans be a bust, too? Unless Marvin Harrison Jr.'s new team can tap back into the production that made him a promising rookie two years ago, the investment of a second-round pick to acquire him will go down as a steep price to pay for no more than a tertiary option in a deep receiving corps.

With time, Harrison's reunion with his college quarterback, C.J. Stroud, may prove fruitful. It would be unfair to ask those two to hit the ground running as a prolific tandem considering their time apart and the amount of time it takes to settle into a new system, but over the long term (and there is a long term here with Harrison under contract through 2027 and potentially into 2028) it is a reasonable expectation. Harrison is still a talented player, and Stroud is rounding into a standout franchise quarterback this season. On paper, those two things should mesh well.

There are warning signs about Harrison's future as a viable NFL starter, though, most notably in the form of his questionable effort in Arizona. And while he does have a touchdown already in Houston, he has not caught more than three passes in a game since joining the Texans and has only run 29 routes over three games. All three of his appearances came off the bench, too.

The modest playing time could be a result of Houston easing him into action until he gets a firm grasp on the playbook and rebuilds his connection with Stroud, but it may also indicate that he is not a top option in what has quickly become a crowded wide receiver group. Stroud has to battle each of these players for targets:

That is not to mention tight end Dalton Schultz, who leads all Texans with 47 targets on the season.

If it pans out, the Kirk Cousins move could be the most impactful in-season trade of them all and spark a Super Bowl run for the Minnesota Vikings. His potential to elevate the offense and maximize the team's potential with its otherworldly defense is real. But there is also a risk that Cousins cannot replicate what he did with the Las Vegas Raiders over the first half of the season, and the Vikings give up a third-round pick for a lateral move at quarterback rather than an upgrade over Kyler Murray.

Cousins was rejuvenated in Sin City and played his best version of football since his first stint in Minnesota. He is even on pace to flirt with the first 40-touchdown season of his career. The 38-year-old who fell out of favor with the Atlanta Falcons turned himself back into a starter and a highly productive one at that. But that came in an immensely quarterback-friendly system that coach Klint Kubiak has proven can turn middle-of-the-road passers into standouts. What happens when he leaves that scheme?

The last time Cousins played for Kevin O'Connell, he made the Pro Bowl. His fit in the Vikings' offense may be just as ideal as the one he displayed in Las Vegas. The numbers, in fact, suggest it could be even better.

But the last time Cousins played for the Minnesota Timberwolves was when he was 35, before he tore his Achilles. This is a different quarterback than the one who won 13 games in his last 17-game season in 2022.

The Dallas Cowboys have only gotten one game of full-strength Joey Porter Jr. despite trading for him all the way back on Oct. 1. He did not record a statistic in that debut. Since then, Porter missed a game due to illness, missed another with an ankle injury, and played through the ankle issue in two other games. It remains to be seen whether he will return to the lineup in Week 10 after he missed last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts.

When he is on the field, Porter is a lockdown cornerback. He allowed no better than a minuscule 47.9 passer rating in any of his first three games with the Cowboys across 10 targets. He still has permitted just one touchdown in his career and has gone 1,570 coverage snaps since then, according to Next Gen Stats. But if he cannot stay in the lineup, he will not be worth the 2028 second-round pick and 2027 sixth-rounder the Cowboys gave up to acquire him from the Pittsburgh Steelers. Especially if he leaves in free agency.

That is the next major question in this marriage between Porter and Dallas. Will he stick around beyond this year? The Steelers were unwilling to meet his reported demands to make him one of the highest-paid cornerbacks in the NFL, and Jerry Jones does not exactly have a history of paying players what they ask for, either. This could turn out to be a one-year rental for a player who has already missed time.

Plus, it is not like the Cowboys' defense at large has taken any major steps forward since Porter joined the unit. The NFL's third-worst group in yards allowed per game remains a stain on what would otherwise be a post-season caliber roster, with its star-studded offense and all.

Similar to the Porter trade, the deal that sent Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts to the Seattle Seahawks has a cloud of uncertainty hanging over it because of a health issue. Nelson underwent a minor procedure to clean up cartilage fragments in his knee and is labeled as week-to-week. He will not play in Week 10 but has also not landed on injured reserve, which indicates he could be back by early December.

Seattle gave up a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to land Nelson on Oct. 27 and thus paid a fairly modest price for one of the top interior offensive linemen of the 2020s. Still, it will only be worth the investment if Nelson gets and stays healthy and upgrades a dormant running game. Before his knee surgery, he did not bring tangible improvement to the ground attack. The Seahawks managed 81 yards in his debut (their second-lowest total of the season) and rushed for a modest 3.6 yards per carry in a slugfest last week.

Nelson's health and ongoing rushing issues have already knocked a few points off the Seahawks' value in what initially seemed like a home-run trade. There is still plenty of time to salvage it, and if he re-signs in free agency, that would go a long way in making the deal age phenomenally. But there is an outcome in which Nelson plays below full strength for most of the year and then leaves in the offseason. In the aggregate, Seattle would be out at least one draft pick (potentially two depending on the compensatory formula) and an All-Pro guard in that case.

#2638. Cooper Flagg beats LeBron James, Anthony Edwards to NBA history: How the Mavericks star leveled up

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

With just over 30 seconds to play on Monday, Naji Marshall missed a free throw that would have put the Dallas Mavericks up by three, but secured the offensive rebound and kicked the ball out to Cooper Flagg. The 2026 Rookie of the Year took some time to assess the situation, then jab-stepped to his right and drove left. He took two dribbles and rose up over Andrew Nembhard, who could do little but hope he missed.

Flagg did not miss. His mid-range jumper was pure and put the Mavericks up by four with 26 seconds left in an eventual 125-122 win over the Indiana Pacers. Flagg, who had been knocked out of the Mavericks' previous matchup with the Pacers this season by a flagrant foul from Aaron Nesmith, finished with a season-high 43 points, 10 rebounds, six assists and three steals on 16 of 25 from the field as the Mavericks won their third game in a row to improve to 7-4.

In the process, Flagg became the first teenager in NBA history to record five 40-point games -- as many as LeBron James and Anthony Edwards combined. No one else besides those three has more than one 40-point game as a teenager. In addition, Flagg is now third all-time in total points scored before turning 20, behind only Kobe Bryant and James. Furthermore, Flagg joined Kevin Durant as the only teenagers to have a 40-point, 10-rebound, five-assist game.

For the season, Flagg is now averaging 25.9 points, 6.9 rebounds, 6.9 assists and 2.2 steals, and that's despite leaving the first game against the Pacers early and an ice-cold 3 of 19 performance against the Sacramento Kings. He's 11th in the league in scoring, 16th in assists and fifth in steals.

"He affects the game in so many ways, and he makes the right plays as far as passing. Thank goodness he's on our team," Mavericks coach Dusty May said after Monday's win. "It's unbelievable he's a 19-year-old doing this."

As May noted, Flagg is far more than just a scorer. But as he continues to establish himself as one of the best young scorers in NBA history, let's take a closer look at how he gets it done in that department.

Flagg is 6-foot-9 and uses his size to get to the basket on a regular basis. He doesn't just bully opponents, though; he plays with a pace that's rare for his age, has great craft around the rim, and is more than willing to move off the ball. You need to look no further than Monday's outing against the Pacers to see how many different ways Flagg can score around the rim.

He forced his way to the rim out of isolation, threw down a dunk in transition, attacked a closeout for another slam, cut back door and spun into another layup, drove to the basket out of the pick-and-roll, cut back door again for an easy finish and ran in transition for a double-clutch lefty finger roll.

Flagg is taking six shots at the rim per game, per Synergy Sports, and shooting 61.7% on them. Among players that have taken at least 50 attempts at the rim this season, Flagg ranks 20th in efficiency.

His ability to get into the paint also helps him earn trips to the free-throw line, where he's shooting 90.3%. Flagg's 7.2 free throw attempts per game rank 12th in the league, and are up from 4.9 per game as a rookie. In his rookie season, Flagg only had eight games with double-digit free throw attempts; he has three already this season.

Flagg put in extensive work on his mid-range game during the offseason, and it's paying major dividends to start the season. Not only has he increased his scoring output, but he's done so while taking less punishment.

"I think just being able to get to my spots at a higher level, and being more comfortable with that, has allowed me to take a little bit of load off my body. Just kind of stopping short, raising up over people," Flagg said on Monday. "It's taxing to get downhill all the way to the rim and try and finish over seven-footers all night, every night. Just adding that in there definitely allows me to pace myself a little bit, steal some easy ones."

Flagg's two clutch buckets late in the win over the Pacers were a perfect example of his improvement.

Flagg is 25 of 42 on off-the-dribble 2-point attempts this season. Among the seven players who have taken at least 40 such attempts, no one has been more efficient. While Flagg isn't going to shoot nearly 60% on pull-up 2s all season, it's clear that he's far more comfortable with his in-between game, which is a great sign for his development.

"He's able to square in the air from 15, 17 feet. He can get to his spots, and if there's a smaller guy he can just jump and square in the air over them," May said.

Flagg's growth inside the arc has allowed him to increase his scoring average by nearly five points per game despite the fact that his 3-point shot remains a work in progress. After shooting 29.5% as a rookie, he's shooting 29.2% this season on slightly more attempts.

Flagg is shooting 30.8% on catch-and-shoot attempts and 31.6% on off-the-dribble attempts. Notably, he's also at just 31.6% on wide-open attempts.

"Like the 3-point percentage obviously hasn't been great, but I still trust myself," Flagg said on Sunday. "I think my teammates trust me, my coaches. So I'm gonna keep shooting it, and I worked on it all summer. I worked on it all last year, so I'm not worried about anything."

Flagg did shoot 38.5% from behind the arc in his lone collegiate season at Duke. That, combined with his elite free throw shooting, suggests that he won't be a sub-30% 3-point shooter forever. If Flagg does eventually become a more reliable shooter, that would be bad news for the rest of the league.

In the last couple of games, he's made some 3s, and he's making all his free throws.

"That's how you put up the 43 points, where you do a little bit of everything," May said after Monday's game. "He finished at the mid-range, he finished at the rim, he got to the line. He's getting to the line more than he has. He affects the game in so many ways, and he makes the right plays as far as passing. Thank goodness he's on our team. It's unbelievable he's a 19-year-old doing this."

#2637. Nikita Kucherov trade request: Five potential landing spots for the reigning NHL MVP

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

One of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey. According to Sportsnet, Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't sign a contract extension and has requested a trade.

Kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era. The 33-year-old just passed the legendary Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead in points and has shown no signs of slowing down.

Just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win. His underlying numbers were even better with a five-on-five goal differential of plus-38 and an expected goals share of 57.0 percent. Only a select few players can drive play from the wing like Kucherov, and that makes him a unicorn of sorts.

Kucherov is in the final year of a contract that pays him $9.5 million per season, and with the salary cap rising rapidly, he's due for a gargantuan raise next summer. It sounds like Kucherov and the Lightning were too far apart on that number, so the superstar winger has shifted his focuse to a change of scenery.

It's important to note that Kucherov has limited trade protection in the form of a 10-team trade list, but that should be more than enough for the Lightning to find a suitable trade partner. With that in mind, let's take a look at five teams that would be ideal fits for Kucherov as he prepares for the next chapter of his illustrious career.

Right out of the gate, this is the most natural fit of all the potential landing spots. General manager Kent Hughes has done a superb job of locking down his young core on team-friendly contracts, and as a result, the Canadiens have nearly $30 million in projected cap space for next season. They also have a glaring need in their top two lines, and I'd say the reigning Hart Trophy winner would fill that role quite nicely.

Montreal's moment to strike is now. It's an ascendant team with a great salary cap situtation and assets to spend. It's time to make a splash, and this would be a tsunami. Just imagine Kucherov on a power play unit with Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Lane Hutson and Ivan Demidov. Kucherov would also be coached by former Lightning teammate Martin St. Louis, so a rapport would already exist between player and coach. I expect the Canadiens to do everything in their power to land Kucherov.

We already know the Wild are big-game hunting at forward because they've been heavily linked to former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin. If I were advising general manager Bill Guerin -- and I'm certainly not -- I would recommend Minnesota package whatever assets it has offered Detroit and redirect them to Tampa Bay. No, Kucherov is not a center,  and that's the Wild's biggest need.

However, Kucherov is a rare breed of winger in that he can drive play better than most first-line centers from the wing. Put him on a line with Kirill Kaprizov, and the only time opponents will touch the puck is when they're pulling out of the net.

With Quinn Hughes also on an expiring contract, acquiring Kucherov would be a risky move for the Wild. What if they give up premium assets only to lose Kucherov and Hughes next summer? I don't think fear can dictate Minnesota's decisions. The team has a top-two defenseman in the world on its roster right now, and it has the opportunity to acquire a top-five forward. Worry about next summer when the time comes. Go all in to win the Cup while you have a chance.

It was no secret that the Hurricanes were in on the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes but just missed out. So, if they can't get better at preventing goals, why not get much better at scoring them? Carolina doesn't exactly need any help offensively, but adding Kucherov would go a long way to helping the team repeat as Stanley Cup champions. Besides, Kucherov would provide another level of playmaking and finishing that the Canes don't currently have on their roster.

Carolina has a good chunk of cap space available already, and it wouldn't need to shed much in order to make room for Kucherov. The Canes also have some enticing young players on their roster that might appeal to the Bolts, and they have three first-round picks over the next two drafts. Why not take a shot at landing a superstar winger?

Similar to the Hurricanes, the Mammoth were in the mix to acquire Hellebucyk, and for good reason. The goaltending tandem of Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa has not been good, so Utah may have to outscore its problems until one of the goalies finds a groove. Offense may be the best defense for the Mammoth -- and if that's the case -- then Kucherov should be in the mix for the Norris Trophy. There is a great young core of forwards in Salt Lake City, and I think Kucherov would be a perfect fit alongside Logan Cooley, who is emerging as a franchise center.

Utah also has plenty of draft capital with which to work, and it's projected for just over $25 million in salary cap space next season. The Mammoth don't have any major pending free agents on their cap sheet, so they're a suitor capable of signing Kucherov to a long-term extension.

Allow me to get a little bold on the fifth and final destination. The Stars have already failed to sign 27-year-old winger Jason Robertson to a long-term extension once. The two sides agreed to a one-year deal worth $12 million prior to the season, but Robertson's future with the team is still very much in doubt. What if Dallas and Tampa Bay executed a true "hockey trade" -- one player for one player?

Dallas would get the better player in Kucherov, but there are no guarantees regarding an extension. The Stars are in win-now mode, and Kucherov could help them get over the Cup hump immediately. Tampa Bay would get a younger player in Robertson, and although he doesn't have the elite playmaking ability of Kucherov, he's still an exceptionally talented scorer. Perhaps the Bolts could get him to join the team's core and sign a multi-year contract. This deal could work for both sides.

#2636. Predicting 2027 MLB Rookie of the Year candidates: Josue De Paula, Kade Anderson, Jesús Made and more

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Tigers infielder Kevin McGonigle and Reds slugger Sal Stewart were named the 2026 Rookies of the Year on Monday night. McGonigle was the wire-to-wire leader for the award despite a stacked American League rookie class. In the National League, Stewart edged out Mets outfielder Carson Benge and Cardinals second baseman JJ Wetherholt, both of whom had excellent rookie campaigns.

No award gets you excited about the future the way Rookie of the Year does. It's a young player being recognized for his greatness, and great young players are what sports hopes are built on. With that in mind, here's a look ahead at the 2027 rookie class and, more importantly, who could be in the running for the 2027 Rookie of the Year awards.

Anderson made his debut in late August and gave the Mariners seven solid starts, though he remains rookie-eligible because he did not exceed the rookie limits of 50 innings or 45 days of service time. Anderson, the No. 3 pick in the 2025 Draft, is arguably the best pitching prospect in the game and is likely to have a rotation spot on Opening Day, which figures to boost his Rookie of the Year case. Add in a pitcher-friendly home ballpark, and Anderson is the super early favorite for the award. He had 167 strikeouts against only 22 walks in 129 innings between MLB and the minors in 2026.

One of the best prospects in the minors, Arias nearly made his MLB debut in September, but the Red Sox opted against it. He authored a .323/.400/.557 line with 25 home runs between Double-A and Triple-A in 2026, including a .331/.388/.506 line in 42 games at Triple-A as a 20-year-old. Trevor Story is entering the final year of his contract and has been healthy and productive at the same time once in the last four years. Arias likely gives Boston a better chance to win right now and I would not be surprised to see them turn the shortstop reins over to the youngster early next season. Early as in April.

Like Anderson, Jenkins made his MLB debut in late August, yet his rookie eligibility remains intact going into 2027. He had a rough go of it in the majors, slashing .226/.293/.393 in 26 games with the Twins, though his contact rates and plate discipline were impressive. Jenkins will turn only 22 in February and he is not the first top prospect to have a rough 26 games to begin his big-league career, nor will he be the last. There might be more growing pains to come next season, but Minnesota figures to give Jenkins a long runway to work through them. His 2027 could look like Benge's 2026, meaning sluggish early and sensational late.

It was only 11 games (plus four pinch-hitting appearances in the postseason), but gosh, De Paula was so impressive during his big-league debut. He's a precocious hitter with tremendous strike zone knowledge (13 walks and five strikeouts), and also some serious hard-hit ability. The biggest obstacle standing between De Paula and next year's Rookie of the Year award is playing time. Shohei Ohtani is locked in at DH and Andy Pages and Kyle Tucker aren't going anywhere. The Dodgers will have to either trade or bench Teoscar Hernández to get De Paula into the lineup. It would be worth it. The Yordan Alvarez comps De Paula got in the minors don't seem so insane now.

The Brewers are the World Series champions and they also have arguably the best farm system in the game with the consensus No. 1 prospect in Made. Still only 19, Made performed admirably in a full season at Double-A this year, and he's currently playing very well against grown men in the Dominican Winter League. He figures to open next season in Triple-A, with a May or June promotion to Milwaukee in the cards. That could put Made at a disadvantage in the Rookie of the Year race. Either way, it's only a matter of time until the defending champions add the game's best prospect to their lineup, presumably at third base.

At 20 years and 121 days, Salas became the youngest catcher to ever appear in a postseason game in Game 2 of this year's Wild Card Series. He started three of San Diego's six postseason games after making his MLB debut in September, and it seems likely Salas will take over as their starting backstop next season. I think he's a longshot Rookie of the Year candidate simply because it's really hard to be a rookie catcher, and next year Salas will be the youngest regular catcher since Hall of Famer Ivan Rodriguez in 1991. Still, Salas is a special defender with promising offensive chops.

Several prominent Japanese veterans will make their way to MLB via the posting system this offseason. We don't know where they will sign yet, but the rules say these players will be Rookie of the Year-eligible regardless of their age or years of experience in Japan, so we're going to include them here.

We ranked Sato as the best position player free agent on the market this offseason. Japan's reigning Triple Crown winner has tremendous left-handed power. We're talking legitimate 30-homer upside. Sato does swing and miss a bunch, though, and he's an aggressive hitter who's unlikely to walk as much as Munetaka Murakami, which could hold him back at the plate. Add in questionable defense at the hot corner and it's unclear exactly how much impact Sato will have in the big leagues. Bottom line though, guys with 30-homer power will always be in the Rookie of the Year conversation.

Taira, our No. 19 free agent, is destined to be a fan favorite given his fire hydrant build (5-foot-8 and 220 lbs.) and bat-missing fastball. He gets close to seven feet of extension down the mound despite his height, creating a unique release window and an "upshoot" effect on his fastball. Taira started for the Seibu Lions in 2026 after spending 2024 and 2025 in the bullpen. I assume the team that signs him will give him a chance to start next year. If he winds up in relief, Taira has the stuff and gumption to get high-leverage outs in the late innings.

#2635. It wouldn't shock me if ... NFL Week 10: Fernando Mendoza struggles in first start, new Chiefs WR dominates

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Nine weeks and the trade deadline are now in our rearview mirror. From here on out, it's all gas no brakes through the second half of the regular season as we rocket towards the playoffs down the road to Super Bowl LXI. Of course, plenty will happen between now and when we kick off that championship match from SoFi Stadium, and we'll keep marching on with Week 10 on deck.

As always, unexpected storylines develop over the course of the season and in a given week, and we try to pinpoint some of them for you here before they arrive.

Last week, we highlighted a bounce-back performance from Bijan Robinson, who had 147 scrimmage yards in a loss to Cincinnati in Madrid. While he didn't commit multiple turnovers, we also put you on the scent of Jayden Daniels -- who fumbled -- being a little loose with the football, along with Jonah Coleman continuing to play well enough to soften Denver's need to acquire a back at the deadline.

We'll look to carry that momentum into this week. Below, you can find five storylines and/or individual performances we wouldn't be shocked to see happen in Week 10.

All NFL odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook.

Rather quietly, Zach Charbonnet has looked good in his return from his ACL tear last January. He's played in two games for Seattle and is quickly taking over the backfield.

After a modest six carries in his first game back in Week 8, Charbonnet dominated the backfield touches in Week 9. The veteran back had 16 carries in the win over Arizona, well above Jadarian Price's 9 carries. On top of getting the lion's share of work, Charbonnet is proving to simply be the better back. He's averaging 4.5 yards per carry, far better than Price's 3.7 yards per carry on the season and 2.8 yards per carry since returning from IR in Week 8.

Given the current trajectory of both players, it wouldn't shock me to see Charbonnet continue to see the bulk of the touches out of the backfield. If he does, he has a chance to put together his best game so far: the Raiders are allowing 5.0 yards per carry this season, which is tied for the most in the NFL.

In fact, Charbonnet is liable to record just the third 100-yard rushing game of his career in this matchup.

Gambling nugget to note: Zach Charbonnet's rushing yards total for Week 10 is 60.5 (-113 to the Over).

Josh Downs was one of the notable names to be moved on deadline day, and the former Colts receiver suddenly finds himself in NFL nirvana. Not only was his trade request granted, but he was traded to the Kansas City Chiefs, where Patrick Mahomes will be his quarterback. Judging by his immediate reaction to the trade on social media, Downs is clearly happy with how things turned out.

I expect the Chiefs to see immediate returns from this move, as Downs fits how the offense has run this season perfectly. More than in any other season of his career, Mahomes and the Chiefs have primarily worked the short passing game, as his 5.6 air yards per attempt highlights. Downs is an elite separator. His 3.2 average yards of separation and +24 yards after the catch over expectation are 24th and tied for 24th among 72 qualified receivers, according to NFL Pro. Mahomes will quickly realize and exploit that ability.

Kansas City has desperately been looking for an answer at receiver as the position group is averaging just 117.5 receiving yards per game this season. Not only does that rank 28th in the NFL this season, but it's the fewest in the Mahomes era. Downs may change that overnight.

Atlanta is coming off a loss to the Bengals in Madrid, where the Cincinnati receivers ran wild. While Ja'Marr Chase is in a class of his own, I do believe Downs can have loads of success against this secondary that also just traded away star safety Jessie Bates.

Finally paired with a quarterback that can get him the football, Downs makes his presence felt early for Kansas City.

Gambling nugget to note: Josh Downs' receiving yard total for Week 10 is 30.5 (-109 to the Over).

The Fernando Mendoza era is about to begin in Las Vegas. The No. 1 overall pick is slated to make his first career start on Sunday, after the Raiders traded Kirk Cousins (who started the first nine games of the season) to the Minnesota Vikings before Tuesday's deadline.

While anticipation is building for a full look at Mendoza in the NFL, this isn't exactly the softest landing spot for him. The Indiana product will have the luxury of being at home, but at the same time will have the tall task of facing the Seattle Seahawks defense.

The unit is allowing just 244.2 total yards of offense per game, including 155.1 passing yards allowed per game. Both are the fewest in the NFL. On top of that, their 4.1 total yards per play allowed is the lowest by any team through nine games since the 2023 Ravens. They're also surrendering the fewest 20-yard plays (17) through nine games since the 2008 Steelers.

Facing the defending Super Bowl champs presents a tough challenge for Mendoza to come out of the gate firing in his first start. In fact, he's the first quarterback taken No. 1 overall to face the defending champions in his first career start. The five previous first-round rookie quarterbacks to debut against the reigning champs have all lost.

Meanwhile, No. 1 pick quarterbacks are 1-15-1 in their first career starts since 2003. Given that history, it's not worth hitting the panic button even if Mendoza does struggle.

Gambling nugget to note: Fernando Mendoza is -156 to throw an interception in Week 10.

Coming into Week 10, Joe Burrow is the odds-on favorite to win the NFL MVP award at +190. He's followed by Josh Allen, who has +250 odds to win the award for the second time in his career. After that, however, is Brock Purdy at +425. By the end of Week 10, however, it's plausible that Purdy ascends to the top of these odds as the new favorite to win the award.

As I've written about elsewhere this week, I think there's a possibility the Steelers cool down Joe Burrow on "Sunday Night Football." To his credit, Burrow has put up otherworldly numbers, but it's come against subpar competition. He faces a much tougher task against Pittsburgh, who is top five in the NFL in yards per play allowed and points per game allowed. The defense is also tied for the eighth-lowest passer rating allowed. Coming off of their bye, while Cincinnati returns from a game in Spain, there's the potential for him to post a dud in primetime, which will ding his odds.

Meanwhile, Purdy gets an advantageous matchup himself as he and the 49ers will roll into AT&T Stadium to face the Cowboys. Dallas is giving up the third-most total yards per game in the NFL and the third-most yards per play. Moreover, they're giving up 26.2 points per game (bottom 10 in the NFL), opponents are converting 48.31% of their third-down opportunities (highest), and a 99.1 passer rating (eighth-highest).

Purdy is top-three in the NFL in completion percentage, yards per attempt, and passer rating this season and has a history of dominating against the Cowboys. For his career, the 49ers QB is 3-0 against Dallas, averaging 9.2 yards per attempt and a 118.4 passer rating.

The stage is set for another monster outing. If he plays to that level, the MVP chatter surrounding him will only get louder.

Speaking of awards, Will Anderson Jr. is becoming the overwhelming favorite to win Defensive Player of the Year in 2026.

Currently, his odds to win DPOY are down to +150, with Fred Warner the next up behind him at +600. That's thanks to Anderson piling up 9.5 sacks, which are the most in the NFL through nine weeks and the second-most by a Texans player in the first eight games of a season (J.J. Watt with 105 in 2012). Anderson is one of the game's elite pass rushers, and I expect him to only bolster his case to win the award with what could be a career performance on Sunday against the Browns.

Cleveland is set to have Deshaun Watson after the veteran quarterback missed last week's loss to New Orleans after landing in concussion protocol. Despite missing a game, Watson still enters Week 10 with a league-high 33 sacks taken this season. Meanwhile, Shedeur Sanders was sacked five times last week. No matter who is under center for the Browns, they get sacked early and often, which is music to Anderson's ears.

The most sacks he's posted in a single game of his career is three, which he's done twice. The first came back in 2024 in a Week 6 game against the Patriots. The second was earlier this year, sacking Cam Ward three times in a Week 5 win over Tennessee. Against a beatable Browns offensive line, Anderson adds another three-sack game to his résumé.

#2634. Albany 'sets the tone' for future after third trip to state in last four years

MONTICELLO, Minn. — On the first play from scrimmage, senior quarterback Cohen Habben pitched an option read into the hands of senior running back Judah Allen for a 35-yard gain against Pierz. That would be the highlight for the Huskies as the Section 8AAA champions were stopped in their tracks against the unbeaten Pioneers, 44-7.

More: Introducing the 2026 St. Cloud Times All-Area Football Team

More: Albany was down 21 points, then Cohen Habben came in at quarterback

"You've got a juggernaut in Pierz," head coach Mike Ellingson said. "I felt like we had our moments and our shots there, and it just didn't transpire for us. Offensively, they're so explosive, but they don't get enough credit defensively for the way they fly around and take away what you do best."

Despite being shut down in the run following Allen's quick gashing run to start the game, the Huskies stayed within reach throughout the first half.

Pierz's Brayden Foust rushed in for the game-opening score from 24 yards out as Preston Saehr connected with Tyler Kimman from 35 yards and Paul Nieman plowed forward from 10 yards to give the Pioneers a 21-0 lead heading into the second quarter.

The Huskies then mounted a drive with the aid of a muffed punt, capped off by a one-yard plunge from senior Dylan Hoffarth to make it 21-7.

After holding the Pioneers to a field goal at the end of the half to trail just 24-7 after a turbulent 24 minutes to start the game, Albany forced a punt to start the second half and had a chance to make some noise.

As Habben scanned the field, a wide-open Emmett Rushmeyer came flying past the Pierz defenders with nothing but green grass ahead. However, as Rushmeyer extended his arms, the ball came just out of reach and would lead to yet another Husky punt.

"It was open in the first half as well and we just missed it," Ellingson said. "Rushmeyer's got some scoot to him, so we took a shot [when] we needed a big play. If we complete that ball, all of a sudden it's a 10-point game. I think the Huskies may make it a different game, right?"

More: Becker girls soccer stopped cold in first trip to state semifinals

More: Sartell boys soccer loses OT heartbreaker in state semis

More: St. Cloud-area runners shine at 2026 MSHSL State Championships

Instead, the Huskies continued to just be another obstacle for the No. 5 team in the state's path to U.S. Bank Stadium.

Foust added another score from 46 yards in the third quarter as Saywer Lochner and Parker Kimman took the final jabs to seal the lopsided victory for Pierz.

"They've got so many dynamic players, and they won the line of scrimmage tonight, too," Ellingson said. "[All night], it looked like a sweep was going to be there for 15 [yards], and that 15-yarder turned into a four-yarder. These kids battled adversity through it all."

Though the Huskies fell short of making it to The Bank, they secured their third sectional title in the last four years and 24th overall while realizing their 13th consecutive winning season, finishing the year with a strong 8-3 record.

"It's a consolation prize, but it's a pretty dang good consolation prize when you make it to this level," Ellingson said. "It sets the tone for the next years, and it sets the tone for the younger guys in the stands being able to go to state and leaves a little bit left to be desired. Making it to The Bank is the next step, and we'll see where that comes in the near future."

#2632. 2026 MLB Rookie of the Year: Tigers' Kevin McGonigle, Reds' Sal Stewart win BBWAA awards

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Kevin McGonigle of the Tigers and Sal Stewart of the Reds were named the 2026 Rookies of the Year in their respective leagues on Monday night as part of the BBWAA's awards week. McGonigle earned 28 of 30 first-place votes, beating out the Guardians' Parker Messick and the Red Sox's Payton Tolle. Stewart, meanwhile, beat the Mets' Carson Benge and the Cardinals' JJ Wetherholt.

Because McGonigle and Stewart were both with the major-league team for long enough to earn a full year of service time, the Tigers and Reds will each receive a Prospect Promotion Incentive pick in the 2027 MLB Draft.

The annual awards, which also include Manager of the Year, Reliever of the Year, Cy Young and MVP, are voted on by 30 members of the Baseball Writers Association of America (that's two per MLB city in each league). Votes were submitted before the beginning of the playoffs, meaning that only regular-season contributions are taken into account.

Stewart won the battle of Old School stats vs. New School stats here. Though he only posted 2.0 WAR, he had 32 home runs and 111 RBI, putting him in rarefied air for a rookie. He's one of just 15 rookies ever with at least 30 homers and 100 RBI. The only names from that list to not win the award either faced another player from the list or played before Rookie of the Year was awarded. Everyone else has taken home the hardware, just as Stewart did Monday evening.

Overall, Stewart appeared in all 162 games, hitting .263/.330/.457 (117 OPS+) with 25 doubles, 32 homers, 112 RBI, 87 runs and 15 steals.

Stewart earned 20 of the 30 available first-place votes.

Carson Benge of the Mets finished second and JJ Wetherholt of the Cardinals finished in third place. Benge, the 2024 first-rounder, made the team out of spring training and hit .282/.346/.430 with 20 home runs, 22 steals and 4.3 WAR. Defensive metrics love Wetherholt and helped push him to 4.5 WAR in 139 games. He hit .242/.339/.365 with 17 homers, 14 steals and 89 runs.

Stewart joins the following Reds as Rookie of the Year winners:

The honor for McGonigle completes a stellar year for the former first-round draft pick. He broke camp with the Tigers and was productive from the get-go. He ended up hitting .278/.376/.430 (126 OPS+) with 28 doubles, five triples, 18 home runs, 72 RBI, 97 runs, 12 steals and 7.1 WAR, the latter good enough for the AL lead among position players. He played great defense, ran the bases well and was an All-Star. He nearly walked (95) as much as he struck out (100), too. Not much more could've been asked of the Pennsylvania native who played most of the season at age 21, and he's a well-deserving Rookie of the Year.

A few weeks after he debuted, he and the team agreed to an eight-year, $150 million extension.

McGonigle won in a blowout, getting 28 of the 30 available first-place votes, scoring 204 of a possible 210 points.

He joins the following players who have won the award with the Tigers:

Parker Messick of the Guardians finishes second after going 12-9 with a 2.56 ERA, 1.06 WHIP and 193 strikeouts in 186 ⅓ innings; he is also a top-three finalist for the Cy Young award. Red Sox starter Payton Tolle finishes third after going 9-6 with a 3.03 ERA (135 ERA+), 1.10 WHIP and 171 strikeouts in 148 ⅔ innings.

#2631. Week 10 Super Bowl stock report: Jaguars go all-in at trade deadline, injuries ravage Patriots offense

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

At the NFL trade deadline, many of the league's fiercest Super Bowl contenders made moves to separate themselves from the pack. The midseason point and the personnel changes that come with it are often a fulcrum upon which the championship race hinges, and that may be the case again in 2026. Teams like the Jacksonville Jaguars and Chicago Bears are pushing their chips forward, and non-competitive teams are feeding them star players in exchange for draft capital.

Some postseason hopefuls were eerily quiet at the deadline, though. Why did the Los Angeles Rams not make a play for a wide receiver? How come the New England Patriots sat on their hands while their offense battles the injury bug? Time will tell whether the decisions to stand pat hurt those teams and others.

Week 10 offers a first look at many players on their new teams, which adds intrigue to a schedule that already includes a couple of massive divisional clashes and an important international matchup.

Here are the latest trends in the Super Bowl race coming out of the trade deadline and heading into Week 10.

James Gladstone had a field day a day before the deadline. The wunderkind general manager pulled off three trades on Nov. 9, which was tied for the most in the league. All of them project to make the Jaguars noticeably better in the immediate future, and one of them, the blockbuster deal for Jordan Davis, added another cornerstone standout to the roster for the long term. Gladstone parted with a first-round pick, two second-rounders and a pair of Day 3 selections to bolster a defense that already ranks second in scoring. That shows a commitment to winning now at the highest level.

Davis and Godchaux will shore up and likely even improve upon the run-stopping efforts while DaVon Hamilton watches the rest of the season from the sidelines with a torn quad. Bates is a plug-and-play replacement for Eric Murray at safety who brings All-Pro-caliber production to the pass defense. The Jaguars filled a couple of lineup holes in an emphatic fashion.

2027 first-round pick, 2029 second-round pick

2027 second-round pick, 2028 fifth-round pick

These newcomers join a team that already holds a three-game lead in its division. They will also line up on the other side of the ball from an offense that is cooking with gas. The fourth-highest-scoring unit in the NFL has flat-out demolished half of its opponents. Trevor Lawrence, somehow, is still somewhat flying under the radar — probably because his offense keeps building such large leads that he does not need to rack up passing numbers in the second halves of these blowouts. Parker Washington has turned into a star, and Bhayshul Tuten emerged as a bona fide No. 1 running back. All of the pieces are in place.

An easy-peasy schedule over the second half of the season paves the way for the Jaguars to contend for the AFC's No. 1 seed. They face the one-win Tennessee Titans twice in the next three weeks, have matchups with three teams from the downtrodden NFC East and close the campaign with a trip to face the rebuilding Indianapolis Colts. The only real test that lies ahead is a Dec. 6 battle with the Bears. That might be a Super Bowl preview.

Just when it seemed like the Patriots were starting to put everything back together, they hit another rough patch. Just like they did to open the season, they have lost two of their last three games. The only win in that stretch was a five-point squeaker against the lowly Miami Dolphins. The road ahead does not get a whole lot easier with five likely playoff teams on the schedule over the next eight weeks. It is going to be a battle to return to the postseason after last year's run to the Super Bowl.

Making matters more challenging is the decimation that occurred on the offensive side of the ball over the last couple of weeks. The Patriots will be without their top two running backs for the foreseeable future as Rhamondre Stevenson battles a knee injury and TreVeyon Henderson manages a mysterious illness. At wide receiver, Romeo Doubs remains on injured reserve, and A.J. Brown cannot seem to get quite right due to his ankle sprain and knee condition. Alijah Vera-Tucker is on IR, too, and represents a key missing piece on the offensive line.

All of those issues undoubtedly contributed to Drake Maye reverting to his early-season tendencies in Week 9. He is back in a tie for the league lead in turnovers on the heels of his three-interception disaster in the blowout loss to the Green Bay Packers.

Because of all these injuries, things might get worse before they get better. If and when the offense gets closer to full strength, time will be of the essence as New England seeks to lock up a playoff berth.

Don't look now, but the Houston Texans are not out of it yet. The AFC South will remain out of reach so long as the Jaguars do not shockingly collapse, so it is Wild Card or bust for a squad that started the year at 0-4. At just 1.5 games back, the Texans are right in the mix.

Since that winless first month of the season, the Texans have won three of four and took two of those games in blowout fashion. They just put up a season-high 44 points on the bottom-dwelling Los Angeles Chargers in a game that emphasized how far C.J. Stroud has come as a quarterback. He continues to play the best football of his career and is not even remotely the reason why the Texans are still two games under .500. Tank Dell's return to the wide receiver group and Marvin Harrison Jr.'s addition about a month ago also gave him a deep stable of pass-catchers to target, and he is cashing in.

Nobody expected the story of the Texans' season to be the offense carrying the defense, but here they are. The defense has to click eventually, right? It is bizarre to watch Will Anderson Jr. lead the league in sacks and play at a Defensive Player of the Year level yet have the rest of the defense fail him. There are plenty of opportunities for that group to right itself against middling opponents in the weeks to come.

Sunday, 1 p.m., Fox, stream on Fubo (try for free)

Losses are rare in the NFC North. At least one team has to add one to their tally in Week 10, though. The Packers are the only team with three losses, so every matchup means a little bit more to them as they try to work their way out of the shallow basement of the NFL's best division — one that could send all four teams to the postseason. They will have vengeance on their minds on Sunday as they seek to get payback for what the Minnesota Vikings did to them in a stunning second-half comeback in Week 1. But they will have to do so against a Vikings offense that should be far better the rest of the season now that Kirk Cousins is in at quarterback.

Considering all of the Patriots' offensive deficiencies, there is a world in which the Detroit Lions post a number New England simply cannot match. But maybe this is the right kind of opponent for Mike Vrabel's squad at this juncture: One with a porous defense that they can move the ball against even when they are not at full strength. Detroit is squarely in the aforementioned NFC North battle and needs a win here, as it does every week, to keep up with the rest of the pack.

Sunday, 8:20 p.m., NBC, stream on Fubo (try for free)

Someone's four-game winning streak has to end on "Sunday Night Football." The victor between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals will secure sole possession of first place in the AFC North. The Steelers got the job done in the first meeting, which was a hotly contested 30-27 clash in Pittsburgh. Home-field advantage means a heck of a lot in this division and could lead to the opposite result this time around. Joe Burrow playing at an MVP level helps quite a lot, too.

#2628. Bob Boone, All-Star catcher, 1980 World Series champion and father of Yankees manager, dies at 78

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Bob Boone, a four-time All-Star catcher and the middle member of a three-generation baseball family, has died. He was 78. His son, Bret Boone, made the announcement on Tuesday. No cause of death was given.

My dad- He was my mentor, my coach, my rock. He taught me how to be a pro and more importantly, how to be a man. He was one of the highest integrity people I’ve ever known and I’m going to miss him dearly. Baseball lost a great one yesterday. R.I.P dad, I love you❤️ pic.twitter.com/4NtYAwXIv3

"Bob Boone had an enduring impact on the field as a 19-year MLB veteran, a seven-time Gold Glove Award-winning catcher, a four-time All-Star and 1980 World Champion with the Philadelphia Phillies," the MLB Players Association said in a statement. "He embraced a leadership role in the Players Association early in his career, and earned a reputation as a strong and principled voice in the advancement of player rights in the 1970s and '80s ... As we honor Bob's legacy and mourn his passing, we extend our heartfelt condolences to his wife, Sue, sons Aaron, Bret and Matt, his extended family, and his many fans and admirers throughout the game."

The Boones were baseball's first three-generation family. Bob's father, Ray Boone, played for six teams from 1948-60, and his sons Aaron and Bret both had long careers spanning the 1990s and 2000s. Bob's other son, Matt, played in the minor leagues.

"I'm just so grateful that I had a dad that took us to work with him all the time," Aaron, now manager of the New York Yankees, said in 2023 (via MLB.com). "He came up at the end of '72, and I was born in the spring of '73. He played until my senior year in high school and literally I was at the ballpark -- my brothers and I, in unis, shagging (fly balls) and doing everything you could possibly imagine. It was a great way to grow up."

Born in San Diego, Bob Boone made his MLB debut with the Phillies in 1972 and took over as the club's starting catcher in 1973. He hit 10 home runs and finished third in the National League Rookie of the Year voting. That started a 17-year run as one of the game's best and most durable catchers. Boone started at least 130 games behind the plate eight times in his career and 110 games 14 times.

With the Phillies in 1980, Boone went 7 for 17 (.412) with four walks and zero strikeouts in Philadelphia's six-game World Series win over the Kansas City Royals.

A seven-time Gold Glove winner, including four straight during his age-38 to -41 seasons, Boone had his most productive years with the Phillies from 1976-79. He hit .282/.351/.414 those four seasons and averaged nine home runs, which was excellent output given the offensive standard at the catcher position during that era. Boone went to four All-Star Games and received MVP votes twice.

"Bob was an incredible player, teammate and family man," the Phillies said in a statement. "He embodied everything we believe exemplary athletes should represent, both on and off the field. We were proud to have him as part of the Phillies family during one of the most historic runs in team history. His impact on our organization, his teammates, and everyone who had the privilege of knowing him will never be forgotten."

Boone ranks second with 2,161 games at catcher during the Modern Era (since 1900), behind only Hall of Famer Ivan Rodriguez (2,377). He is 15th among primary catchers with 1,838 hits and 21st with 2,508 total bases. Boone played parts of 19 big league seasons with the Phillies (1972-81), California Angels (1982-88), and Royals (1989-90).

The Orlando SunRays, a potential expansion franchise, hired Boone to be their manager soon after he retired as a player, though the expansion franchises were instead awarded to Denver and Miami in 1991. Boone later managed the Royals from 1995-97 and the Cincinnati Reds (2001-03). He managed his son, Aaron, those years with the Reds.

In 2005, Boone joined the Washington Nationals as their director of player development and had a hand in building the core that won the franchise's first World Series title in 2019. He remained with the Nationals until 2021. Boone spent five years on the Hall of Fame ballot from 1996 to 2000 but was not voted into Cooperstown.

Owner Steve Cohen is expected to push for Skubal, according to SNY; president of baseball operations David Stearns has long been reluctant to sign big-money, long-term deals for pitchers, though pitchers of Skubal's caliber are rarely available. The Mets are also seeking first base help and bullpen reinforcements.

Nolan McLean and Christian Scott are the only locks for New York's 2027 rotation at the moment. Justin Hagenman, Sean Manaea, Kodai Senga, Zac Thornton, and Jonah Tong are next in line to make starts. Tylor Megill is expected back from Tommy John surgery early next year as well. The Mets have some depth but clearly need more impact.

The Rangers signed Corey Seager to a 10-year, $325 million deal prior to the 2022 season and it paid off quite handsomely with a World Series title in 2023 (Seager was the World Series MVP). With five years and roughly $155 million left on the deal, however, the Rangers appear ready to trade him.

The Rangers "intend to explore moving Seager at the general managers' meetings," reports The Athletic.

Seager, 32, was stellar from 2023 to 2025 in spite of a litany of injuries, averaging 6.2 WAR per season with a .294 average and 158 OPS+. He actually averaged 8.7 WAR per 162 games. Only the injuries kept him from making multiple serious MVP runs. Last season, though, was a step back. In 102 games, he hit .227/.312/.424 with 20 home runs, 51 RBI and 3.1 WAR.

The injury history keeps getting more extensive, too, as he's dealt with injuries to his thumb, hamstring, hip, other hamstring and back in the last four years.

With a lackluster, at best, shortstop class in free agency, now might be the perfect time for the Rangers to move on from Seager, assuming a deal can be worked out with the years and dollars left on his contract. Texas also has Sebastian Walcott, one of the top prospects in baseball, ready in the wings.

The Blue Jays are among the teams with interest in free agent second baseman Brandon Lowe, according to Sportsnet. Ernie Clement, Toronto's primary second baseman in 2026, crashed hard in the second half and has always fit better as a super utility man who plays regularly at different positions. Josh Smith is the team's other second base option.

Lowe would bring needed power to a team that finished dead last in home runs this past season and had just one player, Kazuma Okamoto (33), clear 15 home runs. Only four Blue Jays hit even 10 homers. Also, Toronto's lineup is mostly right-handed. Lowe would add power and also a lefty bat to provide balance. We ranked him as the 13th-best free agent available.

Adding rotation help is a "top priority," White Sox GM Chris Getz said during an MLB Network Radio interview on Tuesday. "We're going to exhaust the starter market, both free agency -- we'll take a look -- along with trades. That is our top priority," Getz said. He also confirmed that Grant Taylor, the team's postseason closer, will move into the rotation. Hagen Smith will remain in the bullpen.

The White Sox have solid enough rotation depth with Taylor joining Sean Burke, Luis Castillo, Anthony Kay, Davis Martin, David Sandlin, Noah Schultz, and perhaps Shane Smith and Drew Thorpe. There is room for improvement, though, particularly at the top. Chicago could use a bona fide ace, not that one is easy to acquire or abundantly available.

Add the Padres to the list of teams that have shown interest in Skubal, reports MLB Network. San Diego has a major need in the rotation -- Joe Musgrove, who hasn't made a start since the 2024 postseason, and Randy Vásquez are their only rotation locks -- and a new ownership group that seems willing to spend in its first offseason.

Skubal is far and away the offseason's best free agent. He is also a Scott Boras client, and, historically, top Boras clients take the largest contract offer regardless of team situation. That isn't to say the Padres are a bad situation. Not at all. They're a very good team that is in the postseason most years, plus they play in San Diego. Who doesn't love San Diego?

The Padres are also connected to several Japanese players, according to The Athletic. That includes MLB free agents Seiya Suzuki and Shota Imanaga, as well as players coming over from Nippon Professional Baseball, like third baseman Teruaki Sato.

Free agent lefty Adrian Morejon is drawing interest as a starting pitcher, but he prefers to remain in the bullpen, according to The Athletic. Even during the season, there were rumblings that Morejon would like to be given a chance to start in 2027. He came up through the minors as a starter and only remained in the bullpen because he was so dominant in a late-inning role.

We ranked Morejon as the offseason's second-best free agent on the idea that he would move into the rotation. The belief within the game is that he has a chance to be an excellent starter, not just a back-end piece. Either way, Morejon is a very good pitcher, and at 28, he's also one of the youngest free agents available. He should have several peak years remaining.

Although they are disinclined to pursue Tarik Skubal, the Cubs hope to add three established starting pitchers this offseason, reports The Athletic. Of the nine pitchers to make at least nine starts for Chicago in 2027, seven are free agents. Only Ben Brown, who recently had neck surgery (per ESPN), and Edward Cabrera, who had a 5.96 ERA and was demoted to the bullpen, remain.

Left-hander Justin Steele is expected back from UCL surgery next year, though he suffered a setback this summer and wasn't able to return as hoped in September. Others like Javier Assad and Jordan Wicks are depth options more than full-time rotation pieces. This free agent class offers plenty of second- and third-tier starters. That's where the Cubs are expected to shop.

Unlike last offseason, the Mets are not interested in a major overhaul despite their disappointing year, reports MLB.com. The Mets went 74-88 and finished in last place in 2026. The only silver lining to the disappointing season was the ability to give a long runway to rookies like Carson Benge and Nolan McLean, both of whom finished in the top four of the Rookie of the Year voting.

The Mets went 83-79 in 2025 and missed the postseason on the final day of the season. They made significant changes last winter, most notably jettisoning stalwarts Pete Alonso and Brandon Nimmo, then had a worse season in 2026. In September, president of baseball operations David Stearns admitted that much turnover created an "uncapped downside scenario," which is executive-speak for "there was too much risk."

Not surprisingly, the Braves are uninterested in moving former National League MVP Ronald Acuña Jr., according to MLB Network. It does feel like Atlanta's offense has gone stale and that they could move a core piece, but it won't be Acuña, nor is it likely to be Drake Baldwin, Michael Harris II, or Matt Olson. Ozzie Albies and Austin Riley are the more obvious players to move. Albies is entering the final season of his wildly team-friendly contract. Riley has six years remaining on his deal, which figures to make a move difficult.

On Monday, Red Sox chief baseball officer Craig Breslow declined to commit to Trevor Story as his starting shortstop next season. "We still have a ton of confidence in Trevor, but any decisions like that are going to take place between Trevor and me far before I speak to anything publicly," Breslow told reporters, including the Boston Globe. Boston has one of the top prospects in the minors in shortstop Franklin Arias, who is very likely to make his debut early next year. Arias could push Story into a utility role or off the team entirely.

#2622. Super Bowl odds: How title odds have changed in nine weeks since the start of the season

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The 2026 NFL regular season is officially halfway through, and it's about time we start paying attention to these division races and the competition for the first-round byes in each conference. The NFC North is completely loaded with every team having at least six wins, while the NFC South features four teams with exactly three victories. The quality of play may be different, but these races will be fierce nonetheless.

What about the Super Bowl favorites? The San Francisco 49ers look like the top dog in the NFC, while the one-loss Buffalo Bills are maintaining pace in the AFC. Let's take a look at the current Super Bowl LXI odds for the teams in the top half of the league, and examine how they've changed from the preseason.

Hindsight is 20/20, but the 49ers may have always been the play in the NFC West and were a good value Super Bowl bet. In a division featuring the reigning Super Bowl champions and an alleged "Super Team," there sat the seemingly-always competitive 49ers. Believe it or not, there were TEN teams that had shorter odds than the 49ers to win the Super Bowl preseason. They were listed at +1900 and are now the favorites at +540.

Through nine weeks, the 49ers are the lone one-loss team in the conference and hold the No. 1 seed. This is San Francisco's best eight-game start since 2019, when they also made the Super Bowl. Brock Purdy ranks top three in completion percentage, yards per attempt and passer rating this year despite the 49ers having the most games missed due to injury among wide receivers (39), according to CBS Sports Research. Injuries are again a concern with the 49ers, as they also have the most games missed due to injury overall with 159. John Lynch added defensive lineman DeForest Buckner and wide receiver Keenan Allen at the trade deadline to fill some holes and should return players like Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and CJ West soon.

Two teams made massive jumps into the top four: the Bears and Jaguars.

The Bears have gone from +2400 to +850 to win the Super Bowl this year. Chicago was coming off a season in which it went 11-6, clinched the NFC North for the first time since 2018 and won its first playoff game since 2011. It certainly looked like Caleb Williams had found his footing in the league, but the Bears were projected to have the hardest strength of schedule in the NFL this season. Each of the past nine teams to enter a season with the hardest strength of schedule failed to win a playoff game. Many saw the Bears regressing in 2026, but they may be even better this season. The Bears are off to their best nine-game start to a season since 2012, boast the No. 3 offense in the NFL and have a rejuvenated defense with the arrival of Jeffery Simmons. The Bears may be the best team in the best division.

The Jaguars, on the other hand, have seen their odds shift from +3000 to +750. Jacksonville is running away with the AFC South, as its six wins this season are as many as the rest of the division combined. The Jaguars are an NFL-best 14-2 over the past 16 games dating back to last year, while Trevor Lawrence leads all quarterbacks in total touchdowns in that timeframe with 42. With the No. 1 seed in the conference in reach, general manager James Gladstone went out and acquired defensive tackle Jordan Davis, defensive tackle Davon Godchaux and safety Jessie Bates III at the trade deadline.

What I will say about the Jaguars is that there are not many impressive wins on their schedule. In Week 3, they blew out the Patriots, who have taken a step back from last year, and beat Joe Burrow and the Bengals in Cincinnati in Week 4. If you were curious, the Jaguars' two losses this season came to the Broncos and Texans. They have an interesting stretch on their schedule from Weeks 13-15, where they play at the Bears, vs. the Steelers and at the Texans.

Since the NFL expanded to 32 teams in 2002, this year marked just the fifth time that we've seen an overwhelming preseason Super Bowl favorite with odds under +1000. The Rams were listed at +550 after loading up on big names like Aaron Donald, Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson, but now own the seventh-shortest odds at +1300.

The Rams are 5-4, and one reason is injuries. Donald and Garrett played together for just the first time this past week, while Matthew Stafford's two star wideouts in Davante Adams (hamstring) and Puka Nacua (knee, turf toe) are now sidelined. Kobie Turner (groin) is on injured reserve, Poona Ford (triceps) and Jaylen Watson (shoulder) are out for the year, and Steve Avila (hamstring) is now expected to miss several weeks.

Even when the Rams were relatively healthy, they haven't looked like the team they were in 2025. To be honest, LA holding +1300 odds at this point is surprising. I would rather place money on the Broncos, Lions, Packers or even Vikings.

#2621. Celtics vs. 76ers winners and losers: Jayson Tatum outduels Jaylen Brown, but Paul George steals the show

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Nick Nurse nailed it. A lot of people had a lot to say in advance of the Celtics and 76ers facing each other for the first time this season, but Philadelphia's coach summed it up pretty well before the two teams tipped off on Tuesday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

"This is probably one -- maybe the one -- that people were circling in the summertime when the schedule came out," Nurse said.

Nick Nurse on his morning conversation with Jaylen Brown and hype surrounding the grudge match with the Celtics.“This is probably one — maybe the one — that people were circling in the summer time when the schedule came out. It’s finally here.” pic.twitter.com/CdBoE576iI

He wasn't kidding. From the moment Jaylen Brown was traded to the Sixers, the hype and drama surrounding the first meeting between him and his old team -- and his longtime running mate-turned-rival, Jayson Tatum -- have been seemingly endless. While Tatum tried to lower the heat on the simmering feud, claiming that he was "caught off guard as much as the rest of the world" when Brown was shipped to Philly, Brown was all too happy to add rhetorical fuel to the fire, saying there might not be beef between the two players, but there was some "lamb chops and gravy" and warning his former teammate to "stay ready at all times."

By Tuesday, there wasn't much left unsaid. When Brown was asked whether he would talk to Tatum prior to the game, he dismissed the idea: "There's nothing to talk about. He's on his side, I'm on my side. We're playing basketball. Both of us are trying to win. So there's nothing to talk about. Check the ball up."

The old saying about being careful what you wish for comes to mind. They checked the ball up and the Celtics ran the Sixers off their floor in what ended up as a blowout 123-101 win for Boston. Aside from the actual victory for the Celtics that moved them ahead of the Sixers in the standings and into first place in the Eastern Conference, here are the winners and losers from the most anticipated game of the season to date, including the under-discussed player in the Brown-to-Philly deal having the performance of the night.

The Sixers beating the Celtics in the first round of the playoffs last year was the outlier, not the rule. Boston tends to get the better of Philly in big games. Tatum and the Celtics reminded everyone about that on Tuesday. He finished with 21 points, six rebounds, four assists and two blocks. And a whole lot of bragging rights.

We got some Tatum vs. Brown one-on-one matchups early, with Tatum getting the better of the duel at the defensive end.

Jayson Tatum forces the turnover on Jaylen Brown in their first iso of the game.📺 NBA on NBC and Peacock pic.twitter.com/IOStW8Kk93

And while his most memorable play didn't come against Brown, Tatum still had the highlight of the evening when he threw down a monster dunk on LeBron James.

JAYSON TATUM WITH THE POSTER ON LEBRON JAMES!📺 NBA on NBC and Peacock pic.twitter.com/LOXzzT0FjJ

Brown was right. There wasn't anything left to talk about. Tatum did his talking on the court.

This was always going to be a zero-sum game. Tatum won, Brown lost. But the way Brown went down wasn't great as far as optics and narratives go. He was held to a season-low 13 points, got in foul trouble, had four turnovers and was a game-worst minus-27. Oof.

Apart from a nice dunk in the first half, it was a game for Brown to forget. Making matters worse, the guy he got traded for had a night to remember.

"I'm a bit frustrated, honestly," Brown said after the game. "I wanted to perform better for my team. Foul trouble kind of derailed me a little bit, but it happens. It's unfortunate, but now we got to just move on to the next."

When the Sixers traded George, it seemed like a magic trick by new president of basketball operations Mike Gansey. George played just 78 largely unspectacular games over two seasons in Philly. Beyond that, he's six years older than Brown and still had two years and more than $110 million left on his deal.

So naturally, George has looked like the best version of himself since leaving Philly and going to Boston. His hot start to the season continued on Tuesday with him dropping 36 points on 14 for 22 shooting from the field, including making six of his 11 3-point attempts. He was so good against his former team that at one point he inspired NBC's Noah Eagle on the play-by-play call to exclaim, "PG-13 has turned Rated R." (Prepackaged, but still a great line.)

PAUL GEORGE HAS 30 POINTSVINTAGE PG. 🔥🔥🔥 pic.twitter.com/AH8RI4yVnp

It was supposed to be either Tatum or Brown's night, but George ended up commanding the biggest spotlight with how well he played. He also got the last laugh after an interaction with a Philly fan who, according to George, "dropped the ball on the ground like I'm a dog to go fetch or go get it instead of passing the ball to me like a normal fan." In response, George said he "rolled him a middle finger."

Looks like Paul George may have also flipped out a fan (or someone) after that three pic.twitter.com/LecXldKldE

With Brad Stevens in the front office and Joe Mazzulla on the sideline, the Celtics have long had a theory of the case: Take more 3s than their opponents and bet that they'll make more. That gamble has served them well more often than not. They won a championship that way while leading the league in 3-point attempts and makes per game during the 2023-24 season. The strategy did not work as well against the Sixers in the last postseason, but the Celtics have made peace with the approach, win or lose.

Nothing has changed. Boston still loves to fire away from deep, and that's exactly what the Celtics did against the Sixers on Tuesday. Boston shot 45% from beyond the arc (22 for 49), compared to just 30% for Philadelphia (11 for 37).

When the outside shots are falling for the Celtics, they're tough to beat. No one knows that better than Jaylen Brown.

Why shake hands or hug when you can just turn your back and offer a cold shoulder instead?

The pregame moment between Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown.📺 NBA on NBC and Peacock pic.twitter.com/P4iclUnqZ5

When asked about this moment, Brown told reporters he "wasn't paying attention" when Tatum attempted to greet him.

"I'm just focused on coming out and doing what's best for my team. Everything else was just, to be honest, I wasn't paying attention," Brown said. "Credit to Jayson, he played well tonight. Credit to the Celtics, they executed, they shot the hell out of the ball and were the better team tonight."

Arguably the best part of Brown ignoring Tatum was Tatum then immediately going to LeBron James for an intricate handshake and embrace right afterward.

Looks like Jayson Tatum tried to dap up/hug Jaylen Brown but it wasn’t reciprocated pic.twitter.com/6iMOrpvmmD

Pretty much everyone was asked about Tatum and Brown, from Joe Mazzulla talking about how the trade could have been handled differently, to Payton Pritchard weighing in on whether there was beef between them, to Paul George taking credit for helping the Sixers "land a future piece" in Brown by getting traded (all the lols there).

The winner, though, was 76ers guard Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, who, unlike Pritchard, didn't try to minimize the suspected animosity between Tatum and Brown -- or at least what appears to be some obvious hurt feelings from Brown's side. When Caldwell-Pope was asked about the situation, he pointed to a social media interaction as proof of what we all suspected anyway.

"I don't know what the tension was before JB left," Caldwell-Pope said. "All I know is when he wrote on the comments when JT did that little interview, that's all I know. That's all I need to know."

Kentavious Caldwell-Pope says Jaylen Brown mindset going into the matchup with the Celtics is he’s trying to BTA:“I don’t know what the tension was before but before JB left all I know is when he wrote on the comments when JT did that little interview, that’s all I know, that’s… pic.twitter.com/Co8Wkh0APS

If you somehow missed it, "that little interview" was Tatum claiming that he found out about the trade when everyone else did -- which prompted Brown to pop up in the comments with a cap emoji, essentially calling Tatum a liar. Credit to Caldwell-Pope for calling it like it is rather than pretending.

Speaking of pretending, Nurse was asked about how Brown was approaching the game and reached into his bag of coach clichés for a classic favored by so many in his profession during times like these.

"He's approaching it as another game," Nurse said. "Big game. He's excited for the opportunity, but he wasn't expressing it in a personal way. He said this is a really good test for our team, and I agree with him."

Nick Nurse on how Jaylen Brown is approaching tonight’s game:“He's approaching it as another game. Big game. He's excited for the opportunity, but he wasn't expressing it in a personal way. He said this is a really good test for our team, and I agree with him.” pic.twitter.com/6MiBQXBVCx

Brown advised Tatum to stay ready at all times and everyone from the fans to the media dined out on the pork chops and gravy remarks for weeks in advance. It's hard to sell that as just another game.

Full marks to whoever came up with the song selection for Celtics shootaround on Tuesday.

Celtics shootaround underway with “why can’t we be friends” playing. pic.twitter.com/EJV3A8pQKL

Not long before tip-off, ESPN's Shams Charania reported that Tatum and Brown had a "heart-to-heart" in France prior to the trade. According to the report, the meeting occurred shortly after Brown was dangled in a failed trade attempt for Giannis Antetokounmpo, but before he was sent to Philadelphia.

That sounded pretty juicy, except to hear longtime NBA guard Evan Turner tell it on social media, "this didn't happen." Not to be outdone, Carmelo Anthony also weighed in on the topic, saying that being around the two in France was "weird."

Carmelo Anthony says the energy was weird with Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown in France when they we're all together just days before the trade happened pic.twitter.com/NQ0rGnt5Vh

Turner's source on the subject was unclear, but he was pretty emphatic about the denial, insisting in the comments to the story that the pair never spoke. Not sure that anyone predicted Turner coming off the top rope to smack down an NBA report, but if this ends with him or Carmelo becoming the new Woj, we're all in for a treat.
